title: The Puzzle that Solves FOUR Different Ways! It's unbelievable ...
description:
Here's where you can try Choose your fav. cage total by Sumanta (ANU): https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/M7JdLN3P98 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Choose a number out of the four numbers 7, 8, 12, and 13. The sum of the digits in each cage is the number you have chosen. Along a thermometer, digits increase from the bulb to the tip. A white dot connects consecutive digits.
There's no answer check, BECAUSE THIS IS FOUR SEPARATE PUZZLES!

title: 2024 Arrives With A Sudoku Miracle
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
With apologies to those of you who might have been hoping for a shorter video on New Year's Eve, Simon tackles one of the most beguiling and brilliant sudokus we've ever seen.  It's called Circled Killers and it's the work of Sparknights, who makes their debut on the channel.  The wit and vision required to set this one are astounding.

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/sparknights/circled-killers

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb end. Digits cannot repeat in a cage and must sum to a number (in the circle) at the cage’s top left corner. A digit that appears in a circle (killer value) indicates how many times that digit appears in all circles. A circle may contain a single-digit or double-digit number but cannot contain a multiple of 10. If it's a double-digit number, then each digit will be separately counted. For example, if a killer value of a cage is 35, then another two 3s and four 5s must be contained in the other killer values; this could be via either a single-digit 3 or 5, or double-digit totals that contain 3 or 5, like 13, 15, 25, 36, etc. No two killer cages of the same size can contain exactly the same combination of digits.

title: A Fabulous Debut Sudoku
description:
This is a great debut puzzle called Per Zip by Anthony Anderson: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/7Q693FQRNj 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits an equal distance from the centre of a lavender 'Zipper Line' must sum to the digit in the middle of that line. Black dots connect digits in a 1:2 ratio. Blue dots connect digits in a 2:3 ratio. Not all dots are necessarily given. The grid contains nine "doublers," one in each row, column, and 3x3 box; each digit from 1-9 is "doubled" exactly once. Doubled digits count as twice their value for the purposes of the zipper lines or dots.

title: Schrödinger's Fog: More Complex Than His Cat!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Here's another sudoku from the seriously impressive gdc and a puzzle that VikingPrime thought might be the best Fog-Of-War sudoku, the best Schrödinger cell sudoku and the best zipper line sudoku!!  Let us know what you think - it's certainly a VERY special one.  (Note that the wording of the rules below (and in the video) has been clarified slightly compared to the wording in the link.)

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/kknb9z9cjy

Rules: 
Place the digits 0-9, once each, into every row, column and 3x3 box. To enable this, one cell in every row, column and 3x3 box is a “Schrödinger cell” that contains two digits. This cell counts as the sum of its digits for the purposes of the zipper line rule below.  Digits an equal distance from the circled centre of a lavender zipper line sum to the same number. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits reveals clues in the surrounding 3x3 area. For the avoidance of doubt, if two strands of the same zipper line enter a single cell then the digit in that cell must be counted twice in determining its contribution to the line.

The Royal Statistical Society's Christmas Quiz is available here:
https://rss.org.uk/RSS/media/File-library/Quiz/RSS-Christmas-Quiz-2023.pdf

Simon's intro today is from Kayleigh by Marillion. "Do you remember...?"!!

title: 2023 Was A Good Year For Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
As we head towards the end of 2023, it's great to see some tribute puzzles emerging.  This one (called 2023!) by Die Hard is a gorgeous play on two of the major sudoku innovations of the year: the "circles" rule and zipper lines.  We love it!

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/t6Rd7d8JD7

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages cannot repeat and must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits an equal distance from the centre of a blue zipper line must sum to the same total. For odd length lines, the total is the digit in the centre of the line. The grey line is a palindrome and must read the same forwards and backwards. A digit on any line also indicates how many times that digit appears on all lines in the puzzle.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It's Boxing Day and we hope you have all had a wonderful festive period with family and friends.

Simon takes on a masterpiece today from IcyFruit called The 12 Regions Of Christmas.  From start to finish, this has so much incredible logic packed into it; this is the ultimate Christmas Stocking filler for a sudoku fan and a puzzle that will live long in the memory.

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/laj1tzweyh

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw 12 orthogonally connected regions of different sizes which do not overlap. The regions do not need to cover the entire grid. Within a region, a digit may only repeat if it appears on a gold ring, in which case it can only appear on gold rings. A digit on a gold ring indicates the number of gold rings within its region. A digit on a pear tree is equal to the number of cells in its region. The 3 digits on red baubles sum to 25.

title: O Christmas Tree: A Yuletide Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Merry Christmas to all of the CtC viewers!  

So many sudokus are recommended to us for the festive period but Cris Moore's Tannenbaumino is the puzzle of choice!  It's full of Cris-tmas cheer and should bring a smile to anyone who has enjoyed a lot of turkey, crackers & brandy butter at lunchtime :)

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/omtjde4f3k

Rules: 
Gather around the tree! Divide the green area into pentominoes, i.e. orthogonally-connected groups of 5 cells. No two pentominoes have the same shape even when rotated or reflected. Digits may not repeat in a pentomino. The tree has ornaments (dots) of several colours. If a pentomino contains a green dot, it is a Germanimo: adjacent pairs of digits inside it differ by at least 5. If it contains a red dot, it is a Renbanimo: it contains 5 consecutive digits. Black, white, and silver dots show a boundary between two pentominoes. Black means their totals are in a 1:2 ratio. White means their totals differ by one. Silver means their totals are equal. Along a thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb end.

Marty Sears is often described as a genius and this sudoku puzzle will do nothing but gather more folk to that opinion! Every single one of the 49 people who have solved it as at the date of publication of this video have rated it 100%.

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/atbh8bj6bp

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Connect each pair of matching coloured spots with a snake. Snakes may only move orthogonally through the grid, not diagonally. They may touch each other (and themselves) but cannot share cells. Each pair of adjacent digits along a snake has the same difference, but this 'difference value' may be different for different snakes. A grey square contains an even digit. A black dot connects two digits with a 1:2 ratio (one is double the other.)

title: The Slowest Snake
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We are so very lucky to have constructors like Dorlir making such incredible puzzles each and every day. The Slowest Snake is just an absolute joy from start to finish - it's the sort of sudoku that can make you gasp, especially when you realise there's no guessing required.

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/vw1q7megqm

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a snake which starts at a grey circle and ends at the other grey circle, and never passes through a grey square. The snake moves orthogonally and/or diagonally and can cross itself and acts as a slow thermometer i.e. reading from one end to the other, digits on the snake increase or stay the same (the direction must be determined by the solver). Furthermore, the snake passes through at least 27 cells. The sum of the digits within a cage must sum to the small clue in the top-left corner of that cage.

title: How To Get Out Of Sudoku Trouble
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The last Oddlyeven puzzle we did was one of the best puzzles we've ever seen (Effervescence).  This one is also magnificent - introducing doublers AND triplers - all resolved with just four lines :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/3hQ4Dmd6q4

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. One cell in every row, column and box is a doubler. This cell counts as double its value on the lines. Each of the digits 1 to 9 appears exactly once in a doubler cell. One cell in every row, column and box is a tripler. This cell counts as triple its value on the lines. Each of the digits 1 to 9 appears exactly once in a tripler cell. Doublers and triplers do not share cells and no doubler or tripler cell is within a king's move of any other doubler or tripler cell. Lines are Region Sum Lines: the values of the digits on each line segment within a different 3x3 box must sum to the same total (say a total of X). If a line passes through a box more than once, each line segment in that box must sum to X separately. Each blue lines may have a different value for X. Eg [the values of] 
r8c1+r9c2+r9c3 = r8c4+r7c4 = r6c4+r6c5+r6c6 = r6c7+r5c7 = r5c6

title: Two Truths And A LOT Of Lies!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

Some people's favourite types of sudoku are "wrogn" puzzles where the clues don't tell the whole truth (or indeed any truth at all!). VikingPrime's Trick Play is one such creation and it's been recommended to us by a number of VERY good setters/solvers.  

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/bgDhfmrfN4

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each of the following standard clue types occurs exactly three times in the grid: Arrow, Circle, Dots, Odd/Even, X/V and Zipper . For each of those clue types, exactly two of the appearances of that clue are correct and the other is incorrect. The "standard" clue types mentioned above are as follows: White dots: Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Black dots: Cells separated by a black dot must be in the ratio of 1:2 (so one digit must be double the other). Arrow: Digits on an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's grey circle. Xs: Cells separated by an X must contain digits summing to 10. Vs: Cells separated by a V must contain digits summing to 5. Odds: Cells containing an opaque grey circle must contain an odd digit. Evens: Cells containing an opaque grey square must contain an even digit. Circle: A digit in a purple circle indicates exactly how many purple circles contain that digit. Zipper: digits an equal distance from the centre of a blue line must sum to the digit in the middle of that line.

title: Islands of Confusion
description:
Here's where you can try Killer Look-and-say Islands by Virtual: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/R8fhNnT2HJ 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Every marked cage is either a Killer cage, a Look-and-Say cage, or both Killer and Look-and-Say. Within Killer cages, digits must not repeat, and must sum to the total given in the top left corner. Within Look-and-Say cages, the ones digit of the number in the top left corner indicates a digit that appears in that cage, and the tens digit indicates how many times the ones digit appears in that cage. For clarity, digits may repeat in Look-and-Say cages even if they are also killer cages. Each cage is a part of an "island" formed of three cages all of size N, where it is possible to reach all three cages by traveling only orthogonally through cages of size N. Within these islands, one cage is a Killer cage, one cage is a Look-and-Say cage, and one cage is both.

title: Why Does He Need A Camera To Solve The Sudoku?!
description:
*** KICKSTARTER - JUST HOURS LEFT ***
There's under 2 days left to get involved with our Kickstarter and secure a wonderful Xmas present for the puzzler in your life (which might be you!):

https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptic-presents-fog-of-war

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We complete the trilogy of sudokus today from Florian Wortmann involving minesweeper clues! The puzzle is called Bridging The Mines but it's more like about five puzzles in one grid.  This one has so much to recommend it and why does Simon need a picture of his screen?!

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/crqk2uytmu

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits joined by a white dot are consecutive. Digits joined by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit must be double the other). Not all dots are given. For each line, one attached circle contains an odd digit and the other circle contains an even digit. The odd digit indicates the number of odd digits along the line (not including itself), and the even digit indicates the number of even digits along the line (not including itself). Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area may be fully shaded or fully unshaded. The circles also act as "minesweeper" clues. Cells containing a circle are always unshaded, and their value is the number of shaded cells in the surrounding 3x3 area (i.e. the up to eight cells that touch the circle either orthogonally or diagonally).

(Just 4 days left on the Kickstarter - link below...)

title: How Can This Sudoku Be Real?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We've had a lot of requests and recommendations for this daunting sudoku from Marty Sears: Everything In Its Right Place.  It has a 100% approval rating and a maximum difficulty rating.  It is also, when you read the rules and think about them for a few moments, absolutely unbelievable that this puzzle can work/exist/be solvable/etc?  One of the great sudokus.

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/pTPD72D9qP

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw 3 snakes which must each begin and end at a different grey spot. Snakes are lines which may move orthogonally and diagonally between cells. They may touch each other (or themselves), and can even cross each other, but they must not branch, share cells with each other, or enter cages. A digit on a snake indicates exactly how many times that digit appears on that snake. Eg: If there is a 5 on a snake, there are five 5s on that snake. One snake is a “German Whisper” line; along it, adjacent digits must differ by at least 5. One snake is a “slow thermometer”; along this line, reading from one end to the other, digits must always increase or stay the same. One snake is “entropic”; along it, any group of 3 adjacent cells must contain one low digit (1, 2 or 3), one medium digit (4, 5 or 6) and one high digit (7, 8 or 9.) Digits in a cage must sum to the small clue given in that cage. Digits separated by a V sum to 5.

title: Our Love Story With Fog-Of-War Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Sandra & Nala's Sudoku Advent Calendar is a treat for all puzzle fans (linked below) and today we tackle the first 9x9 fog-of-war sudoku in the collection.  It's absolutely what we've come to expect from Sandra & Nala - a really lovely solve (and not too difficult) - do try and have a go at it if you have time!

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/p9x40zygp1

Rules: 
It’s the first advent Sunday and we want to go for a walk. Nala doesn’t know where we planned to go yet so it’s a surprise for her and she loves to explore her surroundings! Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Help Nala find the path around the lake by following these rules: The path must be orthogonally connected and visit all cells of all cages. The path forms a loop (ie it has no start or end points). The path can touch itself diagonally, however it is not allowed to touch orthogonally (ie no cell on the path can share edges with more than two other cells on the path). Digits along the path differ by AT MOST 2. Cells separated by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit is double the other). Not all possible dots are given. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells, possibly revealing more clues.


A small tribute in the intro today following the death of Ryan O'Neal. Love Story is a film that means a lot to Simon for family reasons and its hauntingly beautiful music from Francis Lai is rather emotional. There is a slightly longer version available for our patrons on Patreon.

Sandra & Nala's Advent Calendar is (free) here:
https://www.patreon.com/posts/sandra-nalas-93505842

description:
Please - even if you are new to variants - try Clone Squares by Scojo: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/qkrzgnhqew 
Place the digits 1-9 once each in every row, column, and outlined region. There are three sets of clones in the grid, the locations of which must be determined. Each clone is a 3x3 square, and each set consists of three clones. Clones within the same set must contain identical digits in exactly the same positions. Rotations and reflections are not allowed. Clones do not overlap with other clones.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A new Fog Of War sudoku today from Celery called Shadow Circles.  This is a FASCINATING puzzle which requires some original thoughts to find your way through. The two given circles contain the same digit. Digits along a purple arrow sum to the value in the attached circle. Red circles may or may not have arrows attached. title: If You Make A Sudoku Mistake, How Can You Fix It?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A work of art this evening from Miky.  This is one of the most beautiful grids we've seen with an astonishing pinwheel construction that yields some incredible logic.  Now a confession: Simon makes a small pencil-marking error at one point (a card pops up at that moment) but he does realise it later on and fix it. 

Some of you want to know how you unpick an error - well this video is a good example.  It is critical to a) find the error and b) trace through any logical steps after that error to understand what you can and can't rely on from any logic you deduced following the error.  Let us know how you think Simon did.
 
Play the puzzle at the following link:

title: Our Longest Sudoku Solve Ever
description:
*** KICKSTARTER LAUNCHED - FOG OF WAR ***
Check out our new Kickstarter where we tasked ourselves with creating the best Xmas present for a puzzle fan. *** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A couple of weeks ago we released a video in which Simon solved Crux by Jay Dyer.  We've been astonished by how many viewers commented that they prefer these very long solves and so Simon turned his attention earlier this week to Fillomenon by Darth Paradox - another legendary sudoku.

172 minutes later....

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/darth-paradox/fillomenon

Rules:
Draw nine 3x3 boxes within the grid and place the digits 1-9 once into each box. Digits within boxes (the Sudoku digits) must not repeat in any row or column of the grid.

Divide the remaining cells (outside of the nine boxes) into orthogonally contiguous regions and fill them according to Fillomino rules: every cell contains the size of its region, and no two orthogonally adjacent regions may have the same size. No Fillomino region may be larger than nine cells. The clues outside the grid give the sum of the Fillomino digits in the indicated row or column. (Sudoku digits are not included in the sums.) Additionally, a Fillomino digit must not be orthogonally adjacent to an identical Sudoku digit.

Clues inside the grid begin hidden by fog; the fog clears when correct digits are entered. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in the attached circle; all arrows have single-digit sums and do not branch or overlap. Digits separated by a white dot must be consecutive, and digits separated by a black dot must be in a 1:2 ratio; not all dots are given. The purple lines contain a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits in any order.
Rules: 

Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of two neighbouring digits on a grey line is always either 7 or 9.

Have you ever heard of Rally Obedience? It's a type of dog sport that Nala has recently discovered for herself. There is a course to walk and it has signs placed on the ground explaining what tricks to perform before moving on to the next sign. It is a team sport and while Nala is really good at it, her human counterpart gets literally every wrogn on the course. The result: chaos and confusion. We might need help to finish this..

Normal sudoku rules apply. In the final grid all clues need to be wrong. A clue is wrong when the placed digits cause it to be invalid. Placing digits that successfully make clues invalid will help clearing the fog from surrounding cells, possibly revealing more nonsense (clues). Clues are valid if: Digits in a cage sum up to the number on its top left (if given) and do NOT contain repeated digits; digits on arrows sum to the digit in the attached circle. (Each arrow is a separate clue, even if multiple arrows share the same circle); digits on a slow thermometer increase or stay the same as they move from the bulb to the tip; adjacent digits on a green line have a difference of at least 5; adjacent digits on an orange line have a difference of at least 4; digits in an orange shaded circle are odd; digits in a blue shaded square are even; all digits in a (larger) white circle appear in the 4 cells touching it; digits joined by a white dot are consecutive; digits joined by a black dot are in a ratio of 1:2.

title: How Many Galaxies Can You See from Earth? Not This Many!
description:
Here's where you can space out with Galactic Map by Blobz: https://sudokupad.app/blobz/galactic-map 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into galaxies: orthogonally connected groups of cells that have 180-degree rotational symmetry about their centers (marked with a small dot). All cells must be part of a galaxy; no galaxies overlap. 
Grey Dots mark "renban" galaxies: those with two or more cells, whose digits form an unbroken consecutive sequence in any order. White dots mark galaxies of either a single cell, or whose digits do NOT form a sequence. Digits may not repeat within a galaxy. 
As per Galactic Map Standards: All galaxies with at least TWO cells indicate their SMALLEST digit with a diamond icon. All galaxies with at least SIX cells indicate their LARGEST digit with a circle icon.

description:
*** KICKSTARTER LAUNCHED - FOG OF WAR ***

ThePedallingPianist is still busy creating beautiful sudokus aplenty (as well as dealing with new fatherhood!) Here's a lovely idea involving placing three nested Latin Squares into an 8x8 grid - hence the title, Russian Dolls.  Can you discover its secrets?!

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/8nPBD7G8JG

Rules: 
In this puzzle, a Latin Square is defined as an NxN grid of cells that contain only the digits 1 to N where N is greater than 1, in which digits do not repeat in a row or column. This puzzle contains exactly three Latin Squares: one within another within another. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) may not contain the same digit. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive; digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit is double the other).

title: 25 puzzles in ONE Sudoku grid!!
description:
*** KICKSTARTER LAUNCHED - FOG OF WAR ***
Check out our new Kickstarter where we tasked ourselves with creating the best Xmas present for a puzzle fan.  Phistomefel is making a puzzle for it!

https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptic-presents-fog-of-war

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A ridiculous construction today.  This sudoku is literally 25 puzzles in one grid.  How AnalyticalNinja made this we have no idea but we're very glad he did!

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/PPtTtQg476

Rules: 
Digits on arrows sum to the attached circles. Digits within cages can't repeat and sum to the small number in the corner. (or to an even/odd total for certain cages). This puzzle is solved in THREE stages:
Stage 1:
Each 3x3 box is solved independently as a 3x3 “mean mini”. (Each box uses exactly three digits from 1-9 without repeating in the rows or columns of that 3x3 box.)
Stage 2:
Delete all digits except for the central cell of each 3x3 box, then solve each 6x6 quadrant as a “Quattroquadri”. (Place the digits 1-9 once each into the 3x3 boxes such that they don't repeat within rows and columns of the 6x6 bold outlined region)
Stage 3:
Delete all digits except for the sixteen digits saved from Stage 1 and the central four cells of each quattroquadri; this should result in four small X shapes of givens in the grid.
Each 12-cell row, each 12-cell column, and each 6x6 quattroquadri of four 3x3 boxes consists of three sudoku boxes and one mean-mini box.
Each sudoku box contains the digits 1–9 once each. Among the sudoku boxes, digits cannot repeat in the grid’s rows nor columns.
Each mean-mini box can be solved again as mean-minis with one doubler per row and column of the 3x3 box. The doublers don't have to contain different digits.

An alternative link here will test each Stage of the puzzle for correctness and then provide a new url for the next stage:
https://tinyurl.com/bde98nab

title: The New Phistomefel?
description:
*** KICKSTARTER LAUNCHED - FOG OF WAR ***
Check out our new Kickstarter where we tasked ourselves with creating the best Xmas present for a puzzle fan.  Please help us to make this happen!

https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptic-presents-fog-of-war

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
String Quartet by IcyFruit is simply one of the best sudoku puzzles we've ever had the privilege to showcase.  No more words are necessary.  Prepare to be astonished.

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/fGbtDGPpTN

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into 4 sections of orthogonally-connected cells such that each section shares an edge with every other section and no 2x2 area is occupied by only one section. Cells on the same line belong to the same section. Each section has a different constraint, which ALL of its lines must obey. The constraints for each section are: i) RENBAN: Digits on a line do not repeat and form a consecutive set, in any order; ii) PALINDROME: The digits along a line read the same forwards and backwards; iii) GERMAN WHISPER: Adjacent digits on a line must have a difference of at least 5; iv) REGION SUM: Along a line, if it crosses a 3x3 box border, each line segment within a different 3x3 box must sum to the same total. The sum may be different for different lines.

title: These are new sudoku rules.  And I LIKE them!
description:
*** KICKSTARTER LAUNCHED - FOG OF WAR ***
Check out our new Kickstarter where we tasked ourselves with creating the best Xmas present for a puzzle fan.  Please help us to make this happen!

https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptic-presents-fog-of-war

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
zetamath makes brilliant puzzles, often with original rulesets.  Today's sudoku is one such innovation: it's called Nine Rooms and it seems daunting at first but it's actually fairly approachable and quite beautiful.

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/38fLLNhq84

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Cells with a solid grey square contain an even digit.  Cells with a solid grey circle contain an odd digit. The circle or pill in box N records the sum of all the digits within box N that are orthogonally adjacent to the digit N within the box.  Two digit totals are read left to right, top to bottom. For example, the pill in box 6 contains the sum of each digit that is BOTH in box 6 and orthogonally adjacent to the 6 in box 6.

title: Fog-of-War and Schrodinger Cells? What's Not to Love?
description:
Here's where you can play Schrödinger's Foggy Rationale by gdc: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/z9zt7a8ery 
The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits reveals clues in the surrounding 3 by 3 area. "Normal" Schrödinger rules apply: Place the digits 0-9 once each in every row, column and box. Two of the digits will have to share a Schrödinger Cell (S-cell). Each row, column and box contains exactly one S-Cell. S-Cells count as the sum of their digits for all clues. Digits joined by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio i.e. one is double the other. Not all dots are necessarily given.

title: Skiing Through The Sudoku Fog
description:
*** KICKSTARTER LAUNCHED - FOG OF WAR ***
Check out our new Kickstarter where we tasked ourselves with creating the best Xmas present for a puzzle fan.  Please help us to make this happen!

https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptic-presents-fog-of-war

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Ever skied in the fog?  It's a lot less fun than this sudoku from ElChiglia where we have to slalom through the gates in the grid!  It's very entertaining and not too tricky - definitely one to have a go at if you're new to variant sudoku.

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/29nTttfqqt

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Help the skier navigate through the fog. The skier starts at the arrow and needs to pass through all gates (by crossing all Between Lines). The path must run orthogonally between adjacent cells and cannot hit the poles (circles) of the gates. Furthermore, since we are on a steep hill, the path can only go left, right, or down, but never up, and it cannot visit any cell more than once. During his slalom, adjacent cells on the skier’s path oscillate polarity, alternating between low (1234) and high (6789) digits. The slalom gates act as Between Lines. Cells along a line connecting the poles (circles) of a gate must have values between those in the circles. Each gate is exactly 1 cell wide (the line contains only one cell). Additionally, each gate is numbered along the path of the skier, starting at 1. One of the two circles must contain that respective number. Along the path, the gates alternate between being red and blue. The grid is partially covered by fog. When a correct digit is placed, the fog will be lifted from the surrounding cells. Cells connected by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Digits in cells connected by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. Cells connected with an X must contain digits summing to 10.

Normal sudoku rules apply. Every digit that appears in a circle must also appear in at least one of its 4 surrounding cells. title: Christmas Comes Early To Sudoku!
description:
*** KICKSTARTER LAUNCHED - FOG OF WAR ***
Check out our new Kickstarter - launched today - which we're running to create a brand new sudoku phenomenon.  A story by professional writer Peter C Hayward linked with (at least!) 10 brand new Fog-Of-War puzzles by Sandra & Nala; and this all made beautiful by the artwork of Haleigh Mooney.  Please help us to make this happen and create the ultimate nerd Xmas present!!

https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptic-presents-fog-of-war

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Christmas comes early to sudoku today in the form of Sandra & Nala's latest puzzle: Nori Nori Christmas - which also harks back to a video from a couple of years ago in which Simon seemed to have gone mad!!

This is another phenomenal fog sudoku and it's impossible not to smile at some of the logic.

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/2v5h5o63ej

Rules: 
Christmas time is coming soon and it's probably not too early to do some baking! Nala is eager to help out with anything, but she may not be the best fit when it comes to cutting out the cookies and placing them on the tray so they don't touch each other when they go into the oven. She might need some help with that. Would you mind?

Normal sudoku rules apply: Place the digits 1-9 in every row, column and box exactly once each. Digits in a dashed cage must sum to the value in the top left corner of the cage (if given). Digits may not repeat within their own cage. Nori Nori Christmas: Shade exactly two cells in each cage. Each shaded area forms a domino (cookie), not necessarily within a cage. Shaded dominoes may touch diagonally, but not orthogonally. A shaded domino functions as a black Kropki dot, i.e. digits in a shaded domino are in a ratio of 2:1. It is possible for unshaded dominoes to be in a 2:1 ratio.  Digits separated by a white sugar decoration dot are consecutive. Not all possible dots are given. Additionally the grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells, possibly revealing more clues.

title: The Fourth Killer
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Probably the most recommended sudoku of recent months is Marty Sears' The Fourth Killer - a Fog Of War puzzle with a sense of humour and as much wit as you can shake a stick at.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/26w1k7rwci

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Four yellow killer cages are hiding in the fog. Enter correct digits to clear the nearby fog. No guessing is necessary (or allowed!) Digits in a killer cage sum to the small number in the top left corner of that cage. Digits CAN repeat within a cage. In fact, a digit in a cage indicates exactly how many times that digit appears in that cage. Eg a 5 in a cage means that there are five 5s in that cage. Grey lines are bulbless thermometers ie Digits along a grey line must be arranged in ascending order, from one end to the other. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits.

title: The 4x4 Fog Of War Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
ThePedallingPianist's fantastic and imaginative 4x4 Raw Fog Of War sudoku is the sort of puzzle we absolutely love.  You need to think about how to approach it and this yields some surprising logic about how to approach it.  10/10!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/nGb8TFpQ6h

Normal sudoku rules apply.  ie place the digits 1-4, once each, in every row, column and 2x2 box. Some of the grid is covered by fog. Digits along a grey line form a palindrome ie the digits along the line must read the same forwards and backwards. Palindromes move orthogonally and NOT diagonally. title: The First Hardest Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Thank you for even considering watching this extraordinarily long video.  In it, Simon attempts Jay Dyer's sudoku, Crux.  Forgive any slowness of thought throughout the process but this is probably not a very straightforward puzzle.  It is however absolutely baffling that a human being could create this!!  Take a(nother) bow Jay Dyer!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/r89wh6qj90

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid entirely into '15-clumps' - non-overlapping orthogonally connected groups of cells, each of which contains no repeated digits and sums to 15. An arrow in a grid indicates that exactly N 15-clumps can be seen in the direction of the arrow, where N is the digit in the arrow's cell. The arrow's cell is not counted, though that cell's clump may be counted if other cells in it are visible in that direction. Two arrows in the same cell are counted as independent clues.

title: Has This Sudoku Made Him Go Mad?!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
After some astonishing sudokus in recent days, Simon's brain is rendered palindrome-blind by this gorgeous puzzle from CaptZebraCakes.  It's a simple idea: 10-lines and palindromes but the logic feels remarkable fresh (and not easy to this solver at least!).

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/4fxnvktjvn

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a grey palindrome line must read the same forwards and backwards. Each orange 10-line consists of contiguous groups of cells, each of which sums to 10. These groups of cells cannot overlap; every cell is part of exactly one group.  Digits may repeat on a 10-line. Cells separated by a white dot contain consecutive digits.  Not all dots are given.

title: An Education in Puzzles
description:
Lexicon [Look-and-Say Fillomino] by MicroStudy: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/j26Rt4938N 
Fillomino: Divide the grid into regions of orthogonally-connected cells such that no two regions of the same size share an edge. Enter a number into each cell equal to the size of its region. Look-and-Say Cages: Digits can repeat in cages. The number in the top left corner should be read as a look-and-say number and says which digits are in that cage. For example, if a cage has the clue "12" then it means there is one 2 in the cage. If it has the clue "3314" then it means there are three 3s and one 4 in the cage.

title: Learn To Chill In 49 Cells!!
description:
*** SIMON SOLVES CRUX by JAY DYER ***
Join us on Patreon (for as little as $2) for a brand new sudoku hunt from DiMono and Simon's (very very long) solve of Crux (2hours 42minutes).

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Another debut on the channel today for zzw and a beautiful combination of killer sudoku and fillomino called Chillomino.  This has some really original ideas in it and it IS relaxing and fun to solve!!  Loved it.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/MfhQqpqPHt

Rules: 
Divide the grid into regions of orthogonally-connected cells such that regions of the same size don't share an edge. Enter into each cell a number equal to the size of its region. Numbers within cages cannot repeat. If two cages are adjacent, their sums must be adjacent too (in other words, if two cages share an edge, the sum of the numbers in one cage must have a difference of exactly 1 with the sum of the numbers in the other cage.)

[The Answer check will work if you fill in every cell with a number (if that cell contains a single digit).  Any cells that should contain two digits should either be left blank or filled with notation digits.]

title: The Sudoku That Compliments You!!
description:
*** SIMON SOLVES CRUX by JAY DYER ***
Join us on Patreon (for as little as $2) for a brand new sudoku hunt from DiMono and Simon's (very very long) solve of Crux (2hours 42minutes).

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We absolutely love this new fog-of-war sudoku from 99%Sneaky called The Positive Diagonal.  We've had some astonishing puzzle titles recently and this is another legendary one!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/mvuj15iimm

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle. Arrows do not branch or overlap. Adjacent digits along a green line must have a difference of at least 5. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (i.e. one is double the other). Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Not all dots are necessarily given. Digits may not repeat along the marked diagonal. Boxes 1 and 9 are clones, meaning each digit is in the same relative position in both boxes (i.e. if R1C1 is 8, R7C7 must also be 8). Additionally the grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells, possibly revealing more clues.

description:
*** SIMON SOLVES CRUX by JAY DYER ***
Join us on Patreon (for as little as $2) for a brand new sudoku hunt from DiMono and Simon's (very very long) solve of Crux (2hours 42minutes).

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Dorlir has come up with a new and extraordinary ruleset for this one: there are invisible thermometers to find hidden in the yin yang (!).  This feels like a sort of Miracle Sudoku, it's not easy but it is magnificent.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/489rPm6j4f

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 area may be fully shaded or unshaded. Each cell in row 9 reveals how many shaded cells are in that column. Furthermore, in each column the shaded digits in that column, must increase in value, going from either top to bottom or bottom to top. Cells separated by a red dot sum up to 9. A digit on a circle has its value increased by 9.

Today's intro is Damien Rice's I Remember.

If you'd like to experience the ARG mentioned in the video introduction:

title: The Second Hardest Sudoku
description:
*** BRAND NEW SUDOKU HUNT JUST OUT ***
Join us on Patreon (for as little as $2) for a brand new sudoku hunt from DiMono, which released at 4pm yesterday.  It's a story where you need to solve puzzles to access the later chapters :) 

There's also Simon (very very long) solve of Crux mentioned in the video introduction.

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Simon has attempted two sudokus by the extraordinary Jay Dyer today.  One resulted in a video that is 2hr 40mins long (of a puzzle called Crux) and we felt we couldn't inflict this on you.  SO we moved onto Gallimaufry which, while still beautiful, is slightly easier :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/6rPQDFRNh8

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat on the marked diagonal. Digits on a purple line form a set of nonrepeating consecutive digits, which may be in any order. Any three consecutive cells on an orange line must all have different remainders modulo 3 (ie in three consecutive cells there must be one digit from [147], one digit from [258] and one from [369]. Digits along a thermometer line increase from the bulb end. Digits in a cage sum to the indicated total. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit is double the other).

title: The Graveyard Of Schrödinger
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A Halloween-themed masterpiece today from fjam whose sudoku, The Graveyard Of Schrödinger, is an absolute show-stopper! It is a tricky puzzle but it is standout brilliant from start to finish.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/3FJJtfL2Dh

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules almost apply. Place the digits 0-9 into cells such that each digit appears once in every row, column and region. To accommodate this, one cell in each row, column and region is a Schrödinger cell, which contains two digits. In graves (cages), digits must sum to the day, month or year of the date on the grave. Digits cannot repeat within graves. Escape the graveyard by carefully plotting an orthogonally connected path between the green and red cells. The path may not cross the highest or lowest digits in a grave.

If you'd like to try Jane Street's Halloween puzzle before Simon's video tomorrow morning then you can do so here:

title: The Shining Loop Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A debut on the channel (and what a debut!) for ElChiglia and their Shining Loop sudoku.  This has SO many lovely logical ideas and yet can be solved relatively smoothly.  Just wonderful.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/jfrf3mHRbN

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a single non-intersecting loop into the grid by connecting centres of orthogonally adjacent cells. The loop must fulfill the following rules: i) The loop enters every cage exactly once; ii) Within a cage, the loop only passes through cells of the same parity but, when the loop crosses cage borders, the parity of the loop switches; iii) Within each cage, the loop must pass through at least one moon or sun. Each symbol (Moon or Sun) stands for a different parity. Each cell containing that symbol must have the respective parity. Which symbol refers to which parity must be determined by the solver. Digits within cages cannot repeat and must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (if given).

title: A New Type Of Sudoku Fog!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A new twist on Fog Of War sudoku today from Bruce Svare and his puzzle Dense Fog - in which the fog only clears one cell at a time!  It's a very cool idea and has some interesting logic to go with the interesting mechanic.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/gDbhTN8rq8

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Cells separated by a knight’s move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Numbers in white circle quads must appear in at least one of the surrounding cells. A '?' in the quad refers to an unknown number. All numbers in the quad are sorted from smallest to largest left-right, and top-bottom. Example, [1234], [3366]. Duplicates are allowed in a quad. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by a black dot must contain digits in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit must be double the other).  Not all white and black dots are given. Additionally, the grid is covered by a dense fog.  Placing a number in the correct square will reveal ONLY that square.

title: The Sudoku With Six Square Roots!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An absolutely incredible construction today from Jobo and their puzzle Radical Rainbow.  The square root signs each represent a different sudoku constraint and all the sums work!!  This is another of those puzzles that will leave you shaking your head in wonder and admiration for the setter.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/tGd8nT7R6P

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in thick bordered squares must be equal to the square root of the 2-digit number read from top to bottom in the corresponding cage. All squares must contain a different digit. Every square root sign also represents a different constraint. Parity line (red): Adjacent digits along the red line must alternate in parity (odd/even). Entropic line (orange): A set of three sequential cells along the orange line must contain a low [123], middle [456], and high [789] digit. German Whisper line (green): Adjacent digits along the green line must differ by at least 5. Renban (purple): Digits along the purple line are a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits in any order. Region Sum line (blue): Along a blue line, each line segment within a different 3x3 box must sum to the same total. Thermometer (grey): Digits along the thermometer must increase from the bulb to the tip (which are always at the ends of the line); which end is the bulb and which the tip must be deduced.

title: What Sort Of Puzzle Is THIS?!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
One of Simon's favourite types of Japanese logic puzzle is Akari and those clever folk on the Discord server seem to have invented a new form of it!!  The idea is that the lights you place in the grid can be of different colours and this seems to open up a new can of logical worms :)

We try three puzzles tonight: the first (by Sam Cappleman-Lynes) is a basic Akari; the second (by Walker Anderson) is an Akari RGB from the Genuinely Approachable Pencil Puzzle series on the Discord server.  And the main course is Anomalie Bleue from Wisteria Fall - which has been recommended to us many times.

Play the puzzles at the link below:

Sam's puzzle:
https://puzz.link/p?akari/10/10/m.j65bga.ja.k.k.gbbd5.k.k.hch.hbg67dh.m

Walker's puzzle:
https://link.sudokupad.app/walkers-akari

Wisteria Fall's puzzle, Anomalie Bleue:
https://link.sudokupad.app/wisteriafalls-akari

A special thank you to Pedro PSI for developing the Kudamono Player and Editor support that is being used to create and play these puzzles. 

Rules: 
Place lights in some unshaded cells so that every unshaded cell is illuminated. Lights illuminate the cell they’re in as well as all cells seen in a straight line horizontally or vertically up to either the first shaded cell or the edge of the grid. Lights may not illuminate each other. A number in a shaded cell counts the lights orthogonally adjacent to that cell. 

In the Akari(RGB) puzzles the following additional rules apply: 

Each light is either Red, Green or Blue. A clue in an unshaded cell gives the colour resulting from all lights illuminating that cell.

title: My Fail from the Crossword Championship
description:
Here's where you can try Ninety One by NotThatItMatters: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/pHm4JTbr9d 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cage has a value of 91 obtained by Horner's method. If the digits in a cage are A-B-C-D-E, left to right or top to bottom, the value of the cage is 91 = (A * B + C) * D + E. Each cage contains a unique set of digits. The six shaded cells in the top right and the six shaded cells in the bottom left of the grid are each a pair of overlapping 1-9-3-2 snakes. These snakes go orthogonally or diagonally from cell to cell.

title: How Can This Possibly Solve?!
description:
Apologies but tonight’s video was not recorded today.  We’d hoped to bring you an update about the Times Crossword Championship - in which we both managed epic fails - and also to say happy birthdays to Ann-Christin, Carole and Jae but Simon has been affected by a power cut as someone drove their car through a telegraph pole in his area so this is from his (scarce) holiday stash. Hopefully back to normal tomorrow where he’d been intending to do a bonus crossword video about the championship in the morning.

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Another loop-building sudoku today from yttrio and this one is even more astonishing than the last.  A few small cages is all it takes to create a fascinating and jaw-dropping solve path.  It's bizarre and quite wonderful!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/RDQq2T2rpG

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage must not repeat and must sum to the number in the top left corner of the cage. Draw a one-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells. The loop may not touch itself, not even diagonally. The loop must enter at least one cell of each cage. Numbers on the loop count as double their value when calculating cage sums. For example, a 2-cell cage summing to 10 may contain a 2 on the loop and a 6 not on the loop. The loop acts as a German Whispers line (i.e., adjacent digits on the loop must have a difference of at least 5). The original, undoubled value of the digit is always used for the purposes of the German Whispers constraint.

description:
Here's where you can have a go at Heisenberg by Randall: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/FQQf6HQfm7 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in its circle. Digits along an arrow also act as an X-sum “clue”: the following X digits (in the direction of the arrow) sum to the clue, where X is the first cell in that direction. 2-cell arrows are double-digit clues: The nearest digit to the arrow circle is the tens digit, followed by the units digit. The inequality symbol ‘points’ to the smaller of the two digits surrounding the symbol.

title: A Complete Fibonacci Fog!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A fascinating debut on the channel today for Flipsen and their fog of war sudoku "Welcome To Elementary School", which features a unique Fibonacci idea!  As always with Fog Of War it's an absolute blast to work out how to place any digits at all in this one!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/DGjdPjDn9P

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. 9-cell diagonals are Fibonacci lines (in modulo 10) starting with two consecutive digits (eg. 1,2,3,5,8,3,1...). The first digit in a Fibonacci line is always the smaller one. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits with a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit is double the other). Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Digits along an arrow must sum to the total in that arrow´s circle/pill (read as a 2-digit number). Placing correct digits will clear the fog from the surrounding cells. [The modulus 10 of a number is the reminder you get after dividing that number by 10. Ie it is just the units digit on any number! Eg 47 modulo 10 is simply 7. A Fibonacci line is a series of numbers in which each number is the sum of the two preceding numbers.]

title: 33% Of Everything Is WROGN
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
In November 2019 we attempted a puzzle called Two Truths And A Lie by zetamath, which some viewed as the greatest sudoku puzzle ever.  Tallcat has now made a sequel and today we give it a go!  It absolutely lives up to its illustrious predecessor - this is a quite brilliant idea and the execution is ridiculous.  Easy it isn't but wonderful it certainly is.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/F2nGdPj2GH

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. All clue types are standard. However, exactly one instance of every clue type is lying to you! Constraints that do not lie work as follows: 
Between Lines: Cells along lines between two blue circles must have values between those in the circles. 
Black Kropki: Cells separated by a black dot contain digits with a ratio of 1:2. 
Even: A cell with a grey square must contain an even digit. 
German Whispers: Adjacent digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5. 
Odd: A cell with a grey circle must contain an odd digit. 
Renban: Cells along a purple line must contain a set of consecutive digits.
Sandwich: Clues outside the grid give the sum of digits sandwiched between the 1 and 9 in that row/column. 
V: Cells separated by a V must contain digits summing to 5. 
White Kropki: Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. 
X: Cells separated by an X must contain digits summing to 10.

Simon's musical intro today is Why Worry by Dire Straits :)

title: The Astronomy Of Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Some might think that there is little crossover between sudoku and the stars but Scojo's Anti-ratio Astronomy puzzle begs to differ.  This is one of only two sudokus on Logic Masters which has maintained a 100% rating with over 45 solves AND an average difficulty rating... so we wanted to check it out!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/fmDD3m73nh

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into “galaxies”, which are orthogonally connected groups of cells that have 180 degree rotational symmetry about their centres, and do not overlap with other galaxies. All cells must be part of a galaxy. The centre of every galaxy is marked by a red dot. Digits may not repeat within a galaxy. No two adjacent cells in the grid (ie no domino) may have digits that are in a 1:2 ratio.

title: Can You Solve These 5 Simple Equations?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Some months ago we published an Arithmetic Quiz Sudoku by mnasti2, which everyone loved so much they voted for its inclusion in our new book.  Well, here's the SEQUEL!  It's called Arithmetic Quiz Fillomino and it's got all the elegance and wit of the first puzzle but this time bound up in Fillomino form :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/RbbMbjH6rH

Rules: 
Divide the grid into regions of orthogonally connected cells such that no two regions of the same size share an edge. Each cell contains a single digit equal to its region's single digit size. Each numbered row contains an equation in the grey outlines that must be completed. A two-cell pill represents a two digit number.

title: The Trouble With Circular Reasoning Is.... (!)
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Dorlir and Marty Sears have teamed up to create a sudoku that, despite its 96% approval rating, is "criminally underrated" according to one tester.  This is indeed an absolutely incredible puzzle that builds on the works both setters have done previously. Be prepared to question your own brain!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/uy5efqsnus

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a loop (one cell wide) of orthogonally connected cells, which does not touch itself, not even diagonally. Each digit on the loop indicates exactly how many times that digit appears on the loop. Eg: If there's a 5 on the loop, it means there are five 5s on the loop. The loop must pass through the bulb of every thermometer. Digits along a thermometer increase from the bulb end. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive.

title: A Sudoku For Your Mental Health (feat. Ren)  : RULES CORRECTED
description:
*** We made a mistake an originally published this video with the wrong instructions ***
If you wouldn't mind giving this video a "Like", it might help the algorithm not to penalise this upload too much - thank you!!

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The sudoku community has been inspired by the artist Ren to create a free pack of puzzles (linked below) in honour of his new album Sick Boi, which released today. Ren's music documents his own struggles with mental health and tonight's puzzle asks us to find our own motivation!  It's called Beautiful Day and it's an absolutely brilliant Fog Of War sudoku from Sandra & Nala.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/1c1i6cf4wu

Rules: 
When a day - no matter how perfect it is - can only take you so far and the fear of hitting that wall where everything stops to flow grows big enough - it is understandable that you will start to look for another solution to your problems. Once found, everything will flow again in all the different directions that seemed blocked just a moment ago. 

What kind of solution will you seek out when you don't seem to be able to come any further?

Normal sudoku rules apply: Place the digits 1-9 in every row, column and box exactly once each. 

Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. Each arrow has its own colour. Arrows of the same colour are connected. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. Not all possible dots are given. One cell in the grid is your newly found “motivation”. Cells must increase in value as they move away from this point in every straight-line direction (i.e. vertically, horizontally and diagonally) until they reach the edge of the grid. Once found, everything will start to flow again. Additionally the grid is partially covered in fog just as your thinking might be impaired sometimes and not allow clear thoughts. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells, possibly revealing more clues.

Play the free pack of Ren sudokus from ZegreS, Sandra & Nala and Raumplaner here:

title: A Sudoku For Your Mental Health (feat. Ren)
description:
*** APOLOGIES BUT THE INSTRUCTIONS IN THE VIDEO ARE FROM YESTERDAY'S PUZZLE ***
Correct instructions are below and pinned in a comment.  We'll consider re-releasing the video later this evening with instructions corrected depending on feedback.

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The sudoku community has been inspired by the artist Ren to create a free pack of puzzles (linked below) in honour of his new album Sick Boi, which released today. Ren's music documents his own struggles with mental health and tonight's puzzle asks us to find our own motivation!  It's called Beautiful Day and it's an absolutely brilliant Fog Of War sudoku from Sandra & Nala.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/1c1i6cf4wu

Rules: 
When a day - no matter how perfect it is - can only take you so far and the fear of hitting that wall where everything stops to flow grows big enough - it is understandable that you will start to look for another solution to your problems. Once found, everything will flow again in all the different directions that seemed blocked just a moment ago. 

What kind of solution will you seek out when you don't seem to be able to come any further?

Normal sudoku rules apply: Place the digits 1-9 in every row, column and box exactly once each. 

Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. Each arrow has its own colour. Arrows of the same colour are connected. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. Not all possible dots are given. One cell in the grid is your newly found “motivation”. Cells must increase in value as they move away from this point in every straight-line direction (i.e. vertically, horizontally and diagonally) until they reach the edge of the grid. Once found, everything will start to flow again. Additionally the grid is partially covered in fog just as your thinking might be impaired sometimes and not allow clear thoughts. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells, possibly revealing more clues.

title: When Even Digits Float On Odd Digits....
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Another debut on the channel - this time for Groktilian - and their puzzle Phials - which incorporates a fascinating "oil floats on water" idea.  This is a brilliant and original sudoku, which seems to combine many puzzles in one!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/42bJJPR2q4

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on thermometers must increase from the bulb end. Along each marked diagonal digits may not repeat. Digits in cages sum to the small number in the top left corner of the cage, if given. Each cage is either full of "oil" (even digits), full of "water" (odd digits), or a mix of both. In all cases, each "row" within a cage is of just one type (oil or water). Oil floats on water, so even digits will always be in rows above odd digits in mixed cages.

title: How Interesting Can It Be To Count To 3?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Paletron's sudoku, EnTropic Islands, is one of those puzzles where, as you're solving it, you wonder how it can possibly exist.  It seems to have been chiselled out of nature itself. A few circles is all that's required to make this 100%-rated masterpiece work.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/PgPqh88p3j

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Low digits (1, 2, 3), middle digits (4, 5, 6) and high digits (7, 8, 9) are defined as three different entropy groups. Orthogonally connected cells of the same entropy are entropic islands. Digit in a circle indicates the size of the island. An arrow between two cells points to the smaller digit.

title: The Strange & Beautiful Zebra Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A debut on the channel for Lake and their incredible puzzle My Strange Zebra (surely one of the great titles?!)  This sudoku is quite magical: the path is SO good... how can this be one of Lake's first puzzles?!?!?!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/rPNr3q67Rj

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area may be fully shaded or unshaded. When a segment of a grey line is shaded, it acts as a “renban” line. Digits on a renban line form a non-repeating set of consecutive digits, in any order. When a segment of a grey line is unshaded, it acts as a “german whisper” line. Adjacent digits along a german whisper line must have a difference of at least 5. Each german whisper and renban line must be at least 2 cells long.

title: 10 Puzzles In 1 Sudoku!?!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Today's sudoku is actually 10 puzzles in one!  Every 3x3 box must be solved individually without reference to the others before the entire sudoku can be attempted.  It's a very cool idea from AnalyticalNinja called House Par(i)ty and has a 2 star difficulty rating (although it's not THAT easy!)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/FRph2b4g2g

Rules: 
Clues outside the grid are Parity Party clues and give the sum of the digits up to and including the first even digit or up to and including the first odd digit from that side. Single digit clues might give the first digit only. (i.e. a 7 clue could mean the first cell seen contains a 7, the first two cells contain an even and an odd that sum to 7, or the first two cells have a 24 pair and the third cell contains a 1.) Digits within cages cannot repeat, and sum to the small number shown. This puzzle is solved in two stages: Stage 1: Each 3x3 box is solved independently as a 3x3 “mean mini”. (ie each box uses exactly three digits from 1-9 without repeating in the rows or columns of that box.) Outside clues are for the first box seen in this stage (ie they “work” for the box next to the clue). Stage 2: Delete all digits except for the central cell of each 3x3 box. then solve the puzzle as a regular 9x9 sudoku using the remaining digits as givens. Outside clues can now see further than just the first box seen.

https://open.spotify.com/playlist/6rr3sOD3qfmf17OM8XvmaK?si=0992788444cc4424

title: Lines In The Fog: 10/10 Sudoku Artistry
description:
*** ORDER OUR NEW BOOK AT THIS LINK ***
If you would like to get hold of a physical copy of our new book, Cracking The Cryptic's Greatest Hits - Volume 2, there is still a chance.  Visit the link below:

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A fanatastic debut on the channel today from apetersen and their Fog Of War sudoku, Lines In The Fog.  This has some absolutely brilliant ideas in it and is just a joy from start to finish.  There is an outstanding question that Simon would like some help with though - please let us know in the comments if you know the answer!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/FMGPBBt24p

Or with original colours:
https://tinyurl.com/4u8rfhfm

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Correctly entering digits will remove the fog in the surrounding cells. Each line has a distinct colour. Lines do not branch, cross, and only move orthoganally. All lines are renban (ie contain a set of non-repeating consecutive digits, in any order). All lines are “region sum” (ie along a line, each line segment within a different 3x3 box must sum to the same total (N). N may be different for each line.) All lines have a length of 3 or more. One line is also a thermometer and digits will increase from its bulb. (The bulb may be in the middle of the line.)

title: All Kinds of Lines - We Love Line Sudoku!
description:
Here's where you can try 10 (Types of Lines) by Math Pesto: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/Ftfnn4L2tQ 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a circle appear at least once each in the four surrounding cells. From left to right, top to bottom, the following lines have the following properties:
Whisper (green): Adjacent digits differ by 5 or more.
Thermo (gray): Digits increase from the bulb to the end.
Renban (purple): The line contains a set of consecutive digits (not necessarily in order).
Between (gray): Digits on the line are between the values in the circled ends.
Region Sum (blue): Digits on the line have the same sum in each box the line is in.
10 Line (gray): The line consists of one or more contiguous groups of cells, each of which sums to 10. Groups cannot overlap.
Nabner (yellow): No two digits may be consecutive.
Parity (red): Adjacent digits alternate between odd/even parity.
Modular (black): Every set of three sequential digits contains one digit from {1,4,7}, one from {2,5,8}, and one from {3,6,9}.
Entropic (orange): Every set of three sequential digits contains one digit from {1,2,3}, one from {4,5,6}, and one from {7,8,9}.

title: The Impossible Sudoku Project
description:
Here's where you can play Impossible? by Damasosos92: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/LQhq2RNjhj 
Place the digits 0 to 8 once each into the 3x3 boxes. Digits may not repeat in the same row, column, or box of the 6x6 grid. Digits in cages do not repeat. Cages all sum to the same total. All the question marks are different digits from 1 to 6 and act as a full rank clue and a x-sums clue at the same time:
Full rank: considering all rows and columns as 6-digit numbers read from the direction of the clue and ranked from lowest (1) to highest (24), the question mark represents where in the ranking that row/column lies.
X-Sums: the question marks give the sum of the first X digits in their respective row or column, where X is the digit nearest the clue.

title: The "Approachable" Miracle Sudoku
description:
*** LINE SUDOKU IS OUT!!!! ***
Line Sudoku, our new sudoku app, is OUT now on Apple and Android!!  The Steam release will happen shortly too :)

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We are constantly amazed by so-called Miracle Sudokus - puzzles which, at first glance, seem absolutely ridiculous due to the lack of information in the grid.  Sumanta Mukherjee's new one is "approachable" but we don't think it's trivial.  Chalk another win up for these magnificent setters and their incredible imaginations!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/QDrdF8HBqg

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb to the tip. Place 9 straight, vertical thermometers, each of different lengths, in the grid. All the thermometers must start from row 9 of the grid. Ie the thermometers all have their bulbs in row 9. No two 9s in the grid share a diagonal. The clues outside the grid are skyscraper clues ie they indicate how many numbers can be "seen" when looking into the grid along the column. A number is visible only when it is larger than all numbers that appear before it along the line of sight.

title: Do You Have To Guess What's Under The Fog?
description:
*** LINE SUDOKU ***
Line Sudoku, our new sudoku app, may be OUT now... we can't control exactly when the Apple and Android releases happen but it should be at any moment!!  

Line Sudoku is an app we've been working on for over a year and it features sudokus by some of the world's best sudoku setters (including Phistomefel, Clover, Jay Dyer, Qodec, zetamath, etc).
  
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Today we try a new Fog-Of-War sudoku from gdc in which our task is to locate 5-cell renban lines in the grid.  Sounds easy but it's seriously interesting and definitely not trivial to do it properly :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/m3GGq4Ht96

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing correct digits reveals clues in the surrounding 3x3 area. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one is double the other). Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Not all possible dots are given. Digits on a line form a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits - these digits can appear in any order. All lines are exactly 5 cells long, don't branch, don't share cells with other lines and only move orthogonally.

title: The Coloured Circles Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A couple of weeks ago we showcased an absolutely beautiful (but very easy) puzzle based on a new circle constraint.  That puzzle was by Dorlir and here we present the significantly harder (and equally brilliant) follow-up!  Dorlir is a professor of maths so there is a serious intellect behind this one - it's got a perfect 100% rating and is said to be of average difficulty.... but is this true?

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/n4FR3FtL4D

Or if you'd like to try the colour circles version then try this:
https://tinyurl.com/ColoredCircles1

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply (ie place the digits 1-8 once each into every row, column and box). The digit in a lettered cell indicates exactly how many times that digit appears in a cell containing that letter. Eg: a 5 in a C cell indicates that there are exactly five 5s in cells containing the letter C. However, 8 of the lettered cells are naughty; these don’t obey the letter rule. Eg: a 5 in a naughty C cell indicates that there are NOT exactly five 5s in cells containing the letter C. Every row, column and box contains exactly one naughty lettered cell.

title: An Attempt At One Of The All Time Greats
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
On a sad day for Simon he attempts a puzzle that has been recommended to us over and over again over these last months.  It carries the dreaded (or relished!?) 100%-rated 5* difficulty moniker on Logic Masters and is a unique combination of Meidjuluk and Fillomino by Agent.  The central ideas are quite lovely and making the fit together feels absolutely miraculous. 

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/Qtghbj7HtM

Or to use the tinyurl link Simon is playing in the video (which has slightly different grid lines):
https://tinyurl.com/AgentP3rma

Rules: 
Divide the grid into two areas of orthogonally connected cells. One of the areas is a Meidjuluk (N=9), the other is a Fillomino. Divide the Meidjuluk area into 9 regions, one of each size 1 to 9. A Meidjuluk region may not contain repeated numbers, and it may only contain factors of its size (eg a region of size 6 may contain any combination of 1,2,3, and 6, including none of them). Divide the Fillomino area into orthogonally connected regions such that no two Fillomino regions of the same size share an edge, and enter a number into each cell equal to the size of its region.

There is an example puzzle at this link:

https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=000EAG

title: How Hard Can A 4x4 Sudoku Be?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
One of those absolutely fascinating challenges today in the form of a 4x4 "sudoku" from I Love Sleeping and Myxo.  The twist is that no set of digits used to complete one row or column can then be used to complete any other rows/columns, while all rows/columns/boxes sum to the same (unknown) total.  It's a head-wrecker and your challenge is to complete it WITHOUT bifurcation!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/nLjQ8DjNRJ

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules do NOT apply. Fill the grid with digits 1-9, such that no digit repeats in any row, column or box. The set of digits in each row or column is unique, eg. if a row contains the digits 1234, no other row or column may contain exactly those digits. The digits in every row, column and box sum to x, where x has to be determined by the solver. Digits separated by an X sum to 10. Digits separated by a V sum to 5. Not all Xs and Vs are necessarily given.

title: The Newest Type of Sudoku Special Square
description:
Here's where you can try Negative Kropki Arrows by Finn Scherer: 
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/HPgDpfjgFb 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits along each arrow must sum to the digit in the circled cell. A black Kropki dot between cells indicates cell values with a 2:1 ratio. A white Kropki dot between cells indicates cells with consecutive values. Not all dots are shown. However, there are nine cells to which a negative Kropki constraint applies (i.e. the cell must have a black or white dot on its edge for its value to have a 2:1 or consecutive relationship between it and the value of the cell it shares that edge with). One of these negative Kropki cells is contained in each row, column, and 3x3 box in the grid, as well as on each arrow (not in the circled cell). Additionally, they each contain a different digit from the set of the digits 1-9.

title: How To Solve Sudoku Without Cheating ;)
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A new Fog-Of-War sudoku today - this time from Blobz!  The idea of these puzzles is to logically deduce the next digit and thereby clear the fog (not to cheat by entering all the digits into cells until the fog is forced to clear!).

This is a simple gorgeous puzzle with a bit of yin-yang and cave logic thrown in for good measure.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/t7hNLh7tBT

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in large circles must appear in the surrounding 2x2 area. Digits separated by white dots are consecutive. Digits separated by black dots have a 2:1 ratio (ie. one is double the other). Not all such dots are shown. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected and no 2x2 area is fully shaded or unshaded. Digits in caged cells indicate how many cells of the same colour (shaded or unshaded) are seen orthogonally from that position, including itself. The "other" colour blocks vision. All dots lie on the boundary of the Yin-Yang pattern (ie. each dot touches one shaded and one unshaded cell). Finally, the grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells, possibly revealing more clues.

title: How To Blow Your Own Mind
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Occasionally older sudokus are brought to our attention... this one, called Secrets and Lines by Starwarigami, is such a puzzle. It is difficult for us to articulate how incredibly clever we feel this is.  The entire grid is covered in lines and the lines must be one of three types... but we don't know which is which.  It is your mission to uncover the truth!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/MTtdF66hqN

Rules: 
This TOP SECRET sudoku has had all its digits redacted. Every redaction is either a Renban, German Whispers or Anti-Factor line. All I can tell you is that row 1 uses exactly two Renban lines, and every other row, column, and 3x3 box uses at least two different types of line. Digits along a Renban line form a set of non-repeating consecutive digits in any order. Consecutive cells along a German Whispers line contain digits which differ by at least 5. Digits along an Anti-Factor line of length n may not be any multiple or factor of n (other than the digit 1), and must sum to a multiple of n. eg a line of length 4 could not contain 2,4 or 8 (but could contain 1).

*** SIMON SOLVES KURT HUGO SCHNEIDER'S NEW SUDOKU ***

title: The Polarity Loop
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A gorgeous idea from yttrio today in the form of Polarity Loop which is a new pseudo-German-Whispery variant.  This is slightly harder than yesterday's puzzle but definitely not THAT hard so do give it a go if you have a little time :) 

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/38RpDFhqDm

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages cannot repeat and must sum to the small clue given in the upper left corner of the cage. Cells separated by a white dot contain consecutive digits.  Not all dots are necessarily given. Draw a one-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells. The loop may not touch itself, not even diagonally. The loop must occupy all cells of all given cages.
