title: The Foggy Sudoku Nebula
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A chastening sudoku today from gdc in the form of Nabner In The Nebula, an extremely clever and unusual fog of war puzzle.  This one gives Simon no end of trouble and yet, as so often with a top-class sudoku, when you find the right way of thinking about it you can't understand what was difficult.  

Also linked below is @KurtHugoSchneider 's new 6x6 sudoku called x.  Apparently you need to know some sudoku theory in order to solve it quickly!!  Simon's solve will be posted on Patreon over the weekend.

Play the puzzles at the links below:

Nabner In The Nebula by gdc 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/NTdGT2L7Fj

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing correct digits reveals clues in the surrounding 3 by 3 area. All golden lines are "nabner" lines ie they cannot contain repeated digits and no two digits along a line may be consecutive.  Eg if 5 is on a line, 4,5 and 6 cannot appear anywhere else on the line. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the first X digits along that row or column (the 'X-sum'), where X is the first digit seen from the direction of the clue. In addition to any nabner lines revealed as the fog lifts, every X-sum forms a hidden nabner line at least X cells long starting from the cell closest to the clue.

Kurt's 6x6:
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/tNJDm73TjD

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a long diagonal (marked in blue) digits may not repeat. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. The cage clue gives the sum of its cage. x is a number that must be determined.

description:

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Every day seems to bring with it another phenomenal sudoku puzzle at the moment and it's Christounet's turn today to share this 100% rated Who's The Man In The Mirror - which introduces us to "mirrored digits"!

title: New Circle Rules Make Incredible Sudoku Puzzles
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We tackled Circular Reasoning by Marty Sears a couple of days ago and this puzzle by Stimim is rumoured to be even better.  It's called Circles and Thermos and uses the same new circle rules.  This IS a magnificent sudoku that, although it's a variant, feels a bit like a classic in terms of how you have to think.

Also linked below is @KurtHugoSchneider 's new 6x6 sudoku called x.  Apparently you need to know some sudoku theory in order to solve it quickly!!

Play the puzzles at the links below:

Stimim's Circles and Thermos:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/dGL3DgJgJd

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit in a circle indicates exactly how many circles contain that digit. For example, if there is a 5 in any circle, then there are five 5s in circles. Some of the circles are also the bulb of a thermometer, digits must increase as they move away from the bulbs.

Kurt's 6x6:
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/tNJDm73TjD

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a long diagonal (marked in blue) digits may not repeat. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. The cage clue gives the sum of its cage. x is a number that must be determined.

title: That's G In The Corner!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Simon is lost in admiration for today's puzzle: Babbling Brook by Knickolas. It's a variant on region sum lines in which the line divisions are made by yin-yang shading... and it's borderline astonishing.

[Apologies if I have used colour-blind unfriendly colours in today's video. I've been pointed in the direction of the Chrome extension Colourblindly and I fear my choice in the video might make it difficult for Red-Blind (Protanopia) viewers.  I'll try to do better in future.]

Play the puzzles at the links below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/dh9t3PnBQ4

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade the grid using two colours, such that all instances of each colour are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 area is completely one colour. Blue lines must have an equal sum N within each colour they pass through. If a blue line passes through a colour multiple times, each individual pass sums to N. (N can be different for different lines). All lines must cross colours at least once. Cells separated by an X contain digits summing to 10.

title: A Major GAS Leak
description:
Here are the URLs for today's 5 GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles. Hat times are given as (two hats/one hat). Any correct solution gets you a dinosaur. 

GAS 796 – What Next? by Philip Newman https://tinyurl.com/r6rvkm22  
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2aelr2jd
Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid give all digits which are adjacent to nine in the corresponding row or column. (6:00/12:00)

GAS 797 – Diagonal by clover! https://tinyurl.com/5xxmya5d 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=23va33bd 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each marked diagonal contains the digits 1-9 once each. (6:00/11:30)

GAS 798 – Time After Time by Bill Murphy https://tinyurl.com/2rypnswv 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=22j8ygyr
Normal sudoku rules apply. Grey regions are clones and must contain identical digits in identical positions. (6:30/12:00)

GAS 799 – Full Circle by Philip Newman https://tinyurl.com/24fsts2h 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2czepkyg
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in corner circles must appear in the surrounding four cells, in some order. (8:00/16:00)

GAS 800 – Kropki Pairs by clover!  https://tinyurl.com/mzmxjdc9 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=22324hxu
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cells joined by a white dot are consecutive; digits in cells joined by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. Not all dots are necessarily given. (6:30/12:00)

title: Circular Reasoning
description:

Sometimes we get so many recommendations about a puzzle that we just know it's going to be amazing. Marty Sears' Circular Reasoning is one such sudoku.  A simple ruleset consisting of just three sentences and yet the grid is pure magic.  You do not want to miss this one!

Play the puzzles at the links below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/dqNLp6qJHR

Normal sudoku rules apply. A circled digit indicates exactly how many circles contain that digit. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.

title: The 99%-rated Parity Loop Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Paletron features for the second time tonight with an exceptionally good loop sudoku involving parity switches.  This is SUCH an enjoyable puzzle to solve and fully merits all the plaudits and recommendations it's received.  Happy Friday!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/LqdQnHfdnM

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a single closed loop (without branching or crossing) moving orthogonally through centres of some cells in the grid. The loop travels on cells of the same parity and, when it crosses a box border, the parity switches. The loop passes through each circle and the number in the circle counts the number of cells around it which are visited by the loop (including itself, maximum of 9). Cells connected by V sum to 5. Cells connected by X sum to 10.

title: This Trick Can Help Unlock Impossible Sudokus
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Tonight's sudoku has received umpteen recommendations in recent weeks.  Apparently it's the ultimate "nabner" puzzle (a nabner line cannot contain two consecutive digits anywhere along it): it's called Someday We'll Meet Again and it's by Twototenth (not Vera Lynn or Johnny Cash!).

We don't want to spoil anything but do give this a go - it's a quite extraordinary construction with so much fascinating logic.  We're looking forward to the comments on this one!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/JBFRPT7RBF

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Gold lines are "nabner" lines; ie they cannot contain repeated digits and no two digits along a line may be consecutive. Eg If a line contains a 2, there cannot be a 1 or 3 anywhere along the line. Any two lines that cross each other will each proceed straight through the intersection. The inequality points to the smaller of the two digits it separates.

title: The Worst Puzzle I've Ever Been Sent
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
According to its rating on Logic Masters, today's sudoku (Foggy Knight by Die Hard) is an average puzzle with few exceptional features. The truth could not be more different: in our opinion this is one of the most incredible sudoku discoveries ever.  The ruleset is incredible and it's a fog of war puzzle with nothing showing.  Prepare to have your mind blown!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/L8HrDHNbHL

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered by fog and correctly placing digits may reveal additional digits. Each digit satisfies only one of the following conditions: a) It is exactly one chess knight's move away from at least one cell containing the same digit; b) It is in its own 3x3 box (3x3 boxes are arranged in normal reading order. So eg 9 in box 9 meets this condition). c) It is the digit 5. There is one exception: the digit in the very centre of the grid satisfies exactly two conditions. No guessing is required or allowed.

description:
Sorry about the audio! I can't understand why it's so echoey, when it was recorded the same way as yesterday. More study required - apologies! Here's where you can try Between The Skyscrapers by Klausku: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/2tfL7TJhPd 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells along a line between two circles must have values between those in the circles. A digit in a circle is a skyscraper-clue for its row (from the left) AND for its column (from the top), so assuming each digit was a building of its size, the number of buildings that can be seen from the left of the row or the top of the column is given by the clue (taller buildings obscuring smaller ones). The inequality symbol ‘points’ to the lower of the two digits.

title: A Sudoku With No Actual Clues?!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We've had multiple requests and recommendations to attempt today's suduoku: Unique Japanese Sum Sudoku from tesseralis.  The ruleset is extraordinary and it is barely credible that this can "exist"... the only thing we know is that all the clues have to be different... but we're not told any of them.  Strap in for one of the most interesting, difficult and downright brilliant sudokus we've ever seen.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/L42nqPggLN

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits joined by a white dot are consecutive. Japanese sums: Shade some cells in the grid such that the clues outside the grid indicate the sums of the contiguous runs of shaded cells found in that row or column. Multiple runs in the same row or column must be separated by at least one unshaded cell. Each caged cell represents a unique positive number. A question mark can represent any positive number.

title: The Thing
description:
Here is where you can try Thing by Oddlyeven: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/nRLRNDQ28T 
Place 1-6 in each row, column and marked region. One cell in each row, column and box is a doubler. The value of this cell counts as double its digit for the other rules. Each digit appears once in the set of doublers. Digits along an arrow sum to the value in that arrow's circle.  Digits in a black circle must not appear AS VALUES in the surrounding four cells. For example, a black circle containing a 4 excludes both a regular 4 and a doubled 2, but not a doubled 4.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The incredibly brilliant (and reliable) James Sinclair returns today with his latest puzzle Collider - not the Hadron variety but the sudoku version!  We have the suspicion that many of you will LOVE this one - it's that clever!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/qbr94BtQfJ

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. On each diagonal (marked in blue) digits cannot repeat. Some cages show their sums, and digits cannot repeat within a cage. A digit inside a white circle must appear in at least one of the four cells surrounding that circle. Digits in cells with a shaded square must be even. Digits in cells separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit must be double the other).

title: Putting Joy into Sudoku
description:
Please forgive the sound quality/echo ... Here's where you can try "Only even … or even only odd?" by Sujoyku: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/D9fpjbmHRn 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid indicates the value of the sum of all even or all odd digits on the indicated diagonal. If the even digits are counted, no odd digit contributes to the sum and vice versa. Digits in a cage do not repeat, and the clue in a cage indicates the sum of all even digits or of all odd digits which are contained in that cage.

title: Watch The Sudoku Map Unfold!
description:
*** NEW SUDOKU HUNT JUST OUT ***
Join us on Patreon (for as little as $2) for a brand new sudoku hunt (called Lines & Shapes) - it was released at 4pm UK time yesterday. Closing date 20th September :) 

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An enormously popular sudoku today from Niverio called The Caribbean - which makes us wish we were in sunnier climes.  A clever ruleset that feels like it could give rise to other puzzles and a whole series of lovely deductions to find - what more could one want on a Saturday!?

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/P4frHfDRFb

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by an X contain digits summing to 10. Not all Xs are given. Shade some cells in the grid such that all the following conditions are fulfilled: 1) All shaded cells are orthogonally connected, without creating a 2x2 area of shaded cells. 2) Groups of orthogonally connected unshaded cells form ‘islands’. Each island has exactly one circle, and the number in the circle shows the size of the island. Each island contains digits 1 to N without repeats, where N is the size of the island. Each island is of a different size.

title: Tightening the GAS Cap
description:
Here are the URLs for today's 5 GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles. Hat times are given as (two hats/one hat). Any correct solution gets you a dinosaur. 

GAS 786 – Comeback Kid by Bill Murphy https://tinyurl.com/bed8j34b 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=26cn8fy9
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells along a purple line contain a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits in any order. Digits in clues at cell intersections must appear in the surrounding 4 cells.  (9:30/18:00)

GAS 787 – Second Guessing by Philip Newman https://tinyurl.com/5e733x6d 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2y3wt4mf
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages cannot repeat and must sum to the given total. (7:00/12:00)

GAS 788 – XV/Kropki Pairs by clover! https://tinyurl.com/5b4wmakb

title: "I Can't Do This Sudoku."
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An innovative and exceptional sudoku today from Crusader175 who, with the help of Chameleon's amazing software programming, introduces us to a completely revolutionary type of puzzle (see what we did there!).

It's called Wheels On The Bus and this one will have you shaking your heads in admiration.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://yusitnikov.github.io/puzzletv/#wheels-on-the-bus

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells in the same relative position in different 3x3 boxes cannot contain the same digits. (So, for example, the top left cells in each 3x3 box must all be different.) Digits on a circle have to be placed in the same circular order in the four cells that are touched by the circle. The circle has to be rotated 90° clockwise N times from the current position. N is the digit in the cell inside the circle. Eg, if R2C8=6, then R1C8=8 and R2C9=4.

title: The Beautiful Sudoku Mark
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Another fantastic sequel today, this time from zetamath with his puzzle Beauty Mark.  We're not sure whether this is referring to our own Mark or that suspicious Z line in the grid - let us know what you think!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/TnR9996Ltn

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Cells separated by the black dot contain digits in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit will be double the other).  The golden lines are “nabner” lines.  Digits cannot repeat on a nabner line, and nabner lines cannot contain consecutive digits - regardless of order.  Eg. if a line has a 3 anywhere on it, 2 and 4 cannot appear on that line.  The blue lines in the grid are Region Sum Lines. The sum of digits on a blue line must be the same within each 3x3 box the line passes through. Eg r2c3+r3c2+r3c3 [box 1] = r1c4+r1c5+r1c6+r2c6+r2c7 [box 2] = r4c4+r4c5+r4c6 [box 5]

title: Sudoku: Singing the Serpent's Song
description:
Here's where you can play The Song of the Serpent and the Wanderer by Damasosos92: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/hf4Jjm3H3J 
The Sudokuland: Divide the grid into regions, each consisting of nine orthogonally connected cells. Each row, column and region must contain the digits 1 to 9 once each.
The King’s Palace: The shown region is the king’s palace. It is one of the regions in which the grid has to be divided, and so it contains the digits 1 to 9 once each.
The Serpent: Some orthogonally connected cells must be shaded to form a single snake that is one cell wide that does not branch and cannot touch itself, not even diagonally. The snake must contain only odd digits.
The Watchtowers: The digit in a watchtower (the squared cells) says how many snake cells are a knight’s move away from that cell. Those snake cells sum to the number placed in the top-left corner of the watchtower. There is a watchtower in every region of the grid, and the snake cannot pass through any watchtower.
The Spell: Each region of the grid must contain exactly the same number of snake cells.

A spectacular innovation on a classic ruleset today from the duo Pacattack25 and Schwupel.  Their puzzle Subzero features thermometers and Yin Yang rules but these are not normal thermos - they can contain negative values (!) This one will warp your brain (in a good way!)

title: The Miracle Road To 200 - Another Amazing Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We cannot tell you how fun and CLEVER today's sudoku is - you must try it if you have some time.  It's called The Road To 200 and it's by Nordy.  It's been described as a sort of Miracle Sudoku and with good reason: initially it seems ludicrous to think it might solve uniquely, let alone in a nice way... but it DOES!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/gJJJdH8TdN

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits along each blue/purple line multiply to 200. Draw a 1-cell wide, non-branching, orthogonally-connected road that does not touch itself orthogonally (but may diagonally). The two ends of the road are given as circles. The road contains only odd digits, and the digits along the road sum to 200. Except for the circles, the road CANNOT visit any cell that contains a given clue ie the road cannot visit the given digits in R2C9 and R9C1, nor any cell that contains a line segment.

title: The Sudoku Anniversary Sequel
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Today is the anniversary of the first sudoku video we made on Cracking The Cryptic (which was exactly six years ago!) Thank you to everyone who has fallen in love with variant sudokus since that day!!

One of the most intriguing puzzles of the last few months was Xendari's Shade Your Own Sum Lines (link below). And today we have a crack at the sequel: Shade Some More Sum Lines by the same author.  This has been recommended by some of the best judges of a good sudoku out there and, although the rules are a little more complicated, this is a first class follow-up.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/QgtR8b9Mr2

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells in the grid such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected. Within each 3x3 box, every separate orthogonally connected group of shaded cells must sum to N, where N is the same for all boxes. Circles can be shaded or unshaded, and the digit in a circle is the number of shaded cells in its 3x3 box. Squares are shaded, and the digit in a square is the number of shaded cells “seen” horizontally or vertically combined from that cell (including itself), where unshaded cells block vision. Diamonds are unshaded, and the digit in a diamond is the size of the orthogonally connected group of unshaded cells that it belongs to.

Xendari's original puzzle is here:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4TPJ32Aa_tQ

title: The JENGA Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We love it when we're recommended approachable sudokus which still score highly in their "interesting" quotient!  Today's puzzle is called Stack 'em Up, Knock 'em Down and it's by rockratzero and it's themed on the brilliant party game JENGA.  It has just a 1 star difficulty rating and we'd encourage everyone to try this puzzle - especially some of our younger viewers. 

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/ivybocixpa 

https://tinyurl.com/rrz-jenga-sp


Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits connected by white dots are consecutive. Digits connected by black dots are in a 1:2 ratio. Not all dots are necessarily given. JENGA blocks are Killer Cages. Ie The digits within a block must sum to the total (if given) in the top left corner of the block. Some block totals are replaced with the letters JENGA and must be determined by the solver. The values of the letters increase alphabetically. (i.e. A is less than E.) [Note that two blocks have fallen and are skewed, the cage totals and dots apply within the blocks - imagine they only cover the two cells diagonally]

title: "Absolutely Blew Me Away"
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Today's puzzle is absolutely miraculous.  We've tackled many "Build Your Own" sudokus before but this one seems ludicrously under-clued... and yet!!!  It's a debut on the channel for Paletron and comes heavily recommended by the likes of tesseralis and thoughtbyte. 

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/JqgBdhMBbn

Rules: 
Normal Sudoku rules apply. Each coloured circle needs to be connected with its colour pair by a “between line”. Cells along “between lines” must have values between those in that line’s circles. Lines can move in orthogonal AND diagonal directions, but they can't cross nor share cells with each other. Lines are not necessarily unique ie the solver must only be able to draw at least one line of each colour which satisfies all the constraints. Circles also show the number of cells visited by their own coloured line in their immediate neighbourhood (not including the circled cell itself) ie a minesweeper count. So, for example, r1c1 could be a maximum of 3 and r4c4 could be a maximum of 8. Arrows between cells point to the smaller digit.

Last week Simon solved one of the most unusual and interesting puzzles we've seen on the channel: Fillomino 77 by Myxo.  Many of you noted that Myxo had made a spectacular Fog Of War sudoku and today we try that as well!

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/L9M2DLtfrh

Rules: 
Normal Sudoku rules apply. Digits connected by a white dot are consecutive. Digits connected by a black dot are in a ratio of 2:1 (ie one digit will be double the other). Not all dots are necessarily given. Coloured lines in the grid are “Renban” lines. Digits on a Renban line form a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits – these digits can appear in any order. All Renban lines in the grid move orthogonally between neighbouring cells, do not branch and do not overlap each other. Each line has a unique colour. The grid is covered with fog. Correctly placed digits will clear the fog around that cell.

Simon comes to the end of his holidays but gets another holiday treat in the form of the latest puzzle from Jay Dyer, X-Clusivity.  Basically this sudoku is about the different ways you can make sudoku digits sum to 10 - it turns out there are quite a few :)

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/JGG2RDFhJq

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The return of one of our favourite setters (and people in the CtC community) today in the form of Qodec - whose puzzle, Badminton, invokes something called a Parity Mirror to play havoc with our heads. Normal sudoku rules apply. Odd-even parity is reflected across the diagonal running NW-SE. (For example: if R6C2 is odd, R2C6 must also be odd.) The other diagonal running SW-NE must contain the digits 1 to 9 once each. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
This is one of those videos where Simon is very unsure in the beginning whether there will actually end up being a video such is the reputation of the puzzle to be attempted!  It's called Fillomino 77 and it's an extraordinary creation from Myxo.  

We're not sure how to describe this one but do give it some thought - the solution is absolutely incredible. [Editor note: Is Simon a human?]

title: Find A Friend In The Sudoku Fog!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Everybody's favourite new sudoku variant returns today with Sandra and Nala's latest Fog Of War puzzle, Looking For A Friend.  This is an educational puzzle not just because it's an approachable solve but because it was apparently originally published in a slightly different form.  Can you see why it is essential that r5c5 is revealed in the initial grid?  

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://beta.sudokupad.app/lookingforafriend-sandraandnala

[If this link gives you an issue then either try the tinyurl link below or refresh your browser and try again.  You might be using an older version of sudokupad cached in your browser and you need to be using the latest version to make sure it works.]

Or this link if they above gives an issue:

https://tinyurl.com/2y7fl4n3

Rules: 
After it gets dark Nala loves to go outside and look for new friends in our backyard. Will she find one today? Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer increase from the bulb end to the tip. There is only one tip for each thermometer and each thermometer has its own colour. Elements of the same colour are connected. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. Not all possible dots are given. Additionally the grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells, possibly revealing more clues.

title: The Door Around The Corner
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
XeonRisq breaks the mould today with an original and brilliant take on the Numbered Rooms constraint.  It's called The Door Around The Corner and you'll need to prepare for surprises - clues don't seem to work the way one might expect and the logic is highly innovative!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/Q2FPmtQ8FN

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid indicate that that clued digit X has to be placed in the Nth cell in the corresponding direction, where N is the digit placed in the first cell in that direction and N will always refer to the first occurrence of X. The arrow determines the diagonal direction of the clue AND once it hits the edge of the grid, it reflects at 90 degrees and continues until it hits the next edge at which it stops (so there are always nine possible cells for each clue).  Eg if r1c5 was a 6 then r6c2 would be a 5. Any set of three sequential cells along a beige line must contain a low (123), middle (456), and high (789) digit. Any set of three sequential cells along a blue line must NOT contain a low (123), middle (456), and high (789) digit.

title: How Can ONE Sudoku Cell Be ≥ 21?!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
If this puzzle was a gremlin, we read the rules and thought it's Stripe!  The rating on Logic Masters suggests it's closer to Gizmo... :)

It's by Oddlyeven and the title gives away the conundrum, it's called Schrödinger's Doublers!!!!  It's a very small, very brilliant puzzle but which gremlin is it??!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/2hm49qMB8N

Rules: 
Put the digits 0 to 6 – once each, into every row, column and box. To enable this, one cell in every row, column and box is a “Schrödinger cell” that contains two digits. This cell counts as the sum of its digits for the following rules. One cell in every row, column and box is a doubler. This cell counts as double its value for the following rules. Each of the digits 0 to 6 appears exactly once in a doubler cell. The sum of the cell values on a line within a 2x3 box must be the same for each box that line passes through. Eg the values of r4c2+r3c3 = the values of r2c4+r1c4+r2c5

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Bellsita has achieved the extraordinary feat of solving 666 puzzles on the Logic Masters Germany portal - and in just a few months.  To honour this achievement the constructor Christounet made this amazing sudoku: Hells Bells.  This is an absolutely BRILLIANT puzzle so please give it a try if you have some time!

Rules: 
Normalish sudoku rules apply: Every row column and 3x3 box contains the digits 0-9 once each. For example, at least 3 of the 4 cells around the circle in R89C67 must have a value of 6. Blue lines must have an equal sum N within each 3x3 box they pass through. Eg r1c3+r2c3=r1c4+r1c5+r1c6=r1c7+r2c7. If a line re-enters a 3x3 box, each segment sums to N separately. Different lines may have different values for N.

title: Phistomefel's Sequel
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A couple of months ago we tacked Chequered Arromino #1 by the mighty Phistomefel.  This was teased as the appetiser of the main course and it's that main course that Simon takes on today. Chequered Arromino #2 is exactly what you might expect: baffling, innovative and quite brilliant.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/mhrHGrTnrM

Rules: 
Divide the grid into ominoes (regions of orthogonally connected cells), so that no two ominoes of the same size share an edge. Each cell contains a number equal to its omino's size. After the regions are placed, it must be possible to shade the regions one of two colours such that any two regions touching on an edge have different colouring. One or more arrows in a cell indicate that the number in the cell equals the number of cells of the same shading in all of the directions combined.

title: The Logic I Missed: An Apology
description:
In last night's video covering the astonishing puzzle Coordi-Loop by Celery, I missed an important and interesting possibility about 20 minutes or so into my solve.  I apologise to Celery for not seeing it especially as I was then unable to showcase even more clever stuff that was packed into this sudoku.  And obviously I also apologise to all the viewers who spotted my error and for whom the video must have been hard to watch.  

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We've been receiving more and more recommendations to look at this puzzle over the last few days.  It's called Coordi-Loop and it's by Celery.  It is difficult to put into words how good this sudoku is.  The whole solving experience is quite unique and some of the deductions available will blow your mind.  Well well worth the effort!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/TqHHLMgRNh

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a loop that travels around the grid orthogonally through the centre of cells. This loop must pass through each 3x3 box at least once. No 2x2 area can fully contain loop cells and adjacent digits upon the loop must differ by at least 5. In a cage digits must sum to the total (z) in the top left corner of the cage if given. Additionally, each cage will reveal a coordinate (Row X Column Y, with X being the uppermost/leftmost digit and Y being the lowermost/rightmost digit) whereby Z must be placed. Each cage's coordinate cell must be part of the loop, and cages are allowed to reference the same cell multiple times throughout the puzzle. The given '6' cage is unique; no other cage can sum to 6!

title: THIS Is One Of The Most Incredible Sudokus Ever
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We've been receiving more and more recommendations to look at this puzzle over the last few days.  It's called Coordi-Loop and it's by Celery.  It is difficult to put into words how good this sudoku is.  The whole solving experience is quite unique and some of the deductions available will blow your mind.  Well well worth the effort!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/TqHHLMgRNh

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a loop that travels around the grid orthogonally through the centre of cells. This loop must pass through each 3x3 box at least once. No 2x2 area can fully contain loop cells and adjacent digits upon the loop must differ by at least 5. In a cage digits must sum to the total (z) in the top left corner of the cage if given. Additionally, each cage will reveal a coordinate (Row X Column Y, with X being the uppermost/leftmost digit and Y being the lowermost/rightmost digit) whereby Z must be placed. Each cage's coordinate cell must be part of the loop, and cages are allowed to reference the same cell multiple times throughout the puzzle. The given '6' cage is unique; no other cage can sum to 6!

title: With Us ... You DO Belong!
description:
Here's where you can try You Don't Belong  by Tambooch: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/MQ6G6HmMbb 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Consider a digit in a cell to be X. In the region immediately around (and including) that cell (maximum 9 cells), there are a number of cells that have the parity of X. If that number is equal to X and odd, there will be a circle in the cell. If that number is equal to X and even, there will be a square in the cell. All digits from 1-9 appear on either a blue circle or square at least once. All blue circles and squares ARE given!

title: A Weird and WONDERFUL Ruleset
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Agent specialises in perfect puzzles and here is yet another.  A completely novel ruleset that seems to borrow from the logic puzzle Coral which works just wonderfully. Here is a sudoku adored by many of the great and good of the sudoku world - try to have a go at it if you have time!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://tinyurl.com/4snw3urc

Or the link below if you cannot use tinyurl (also the link below has a slightly fuller ruleset).

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/bDT6PRQrjR

Rules: 
Each row, each column and each region must contain the digits 1 to 9 once each. Regions consist of nine orthogonally connected cells and must be determined by the solver. Clues outside the grid indicate the sum of digits in each contiguous segment of cells that belong to the same region in that row/column, in ascending order (not necessarily in the order of appearance). Ie the largest clue will appear in the pill closest to the grid. For a given row or column, either all clues or no clues are given. Note that the same region can be represented in multiple pills in a row/column, as long as there's at least one cell in another region between.

title: Dumb and Dumber ... or Hard and Harder?
description:
Here's where you can try the remarkable snake puzzle Slang and Slanger by Darren Nakamura: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/2QNN8rFGnj 
Normal sudoku rules apply. There is a snake (a one-cell wide path) in the grid that moves orthogonally and may touch itself diagonally but may not touch itself orthogonally. The head and tail of the snake are given by circles. Cells in the grid are either on the snake or in one of several non-snake regions (groups of orthogonally connected cells that are bordered by snake cells and/or the edges of the grid). A digit in a square gives the number of cells in that square's non-snake region. Digits on the snake are subject to the following constraints: Within each 3x3 box, adjacent digits on the snake must have a difference of at least 5. Across the bold border between two 3x3 boxes, adjacent digits on the snake must have a difference of at least 4.

title: What Are THOSE In The Sudoku Fog?!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Everybody's favourite new sudoku variant returns today with Sandra and Nala's latest Fog Of War puzzle, Missing Shoes.  This is just a fantastic solving experience that uses double arrows to great effect.  

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://beta.sudokupad.app/missingshoes-sandraandnala

[If this link gives you an issue then either try the tinyurl link below or refresh your browser and try again.  You might be using an older version of sudokupad cached in your browser and you need to be using the latest version to make sure it works.]

Or this link if they above gives an issue:
https://tinyurl.com/2mxpjrdx

Rules: 
Nala has a tendency to pick the first thing she can find that looks "toy-ish“ when she wants to play. In this case she took a pair of shoes and they’ve been missing since. Can you help us find them? Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits along a "double arrow“ (ie a line) is equal to the sum of the digits in the circles attached to either end of the line. Each double arrow has its own colour. Elements of the same colour are connected. Digits in killer cages sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (if given) and cannot repeat. Each killer cage has its own colour. Elements of the same colour are connected. Additionally the grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells, possibly revealing more clues. (And a pair of missing shoes)!

title: Is There ANYTHING Cleverer On YouTube?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
After the pyrotechnics with prime numbers yesterday, today we feature a puzzle that should go down in the sudoku annals as one of the greatest/cleverest we've ever seen.  It's called Galactic Whispers and it's the work of Knickolas, who wowed us a few months ago with Chaotic Equality.  This combines the spiral galaxies logic problem with German Whispers sudoku in a quite astonishing manner.  If you know of ANYTHING cleverer than this puzzle on YouTube then please link it in the comments!!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/H26FG6Bnjp

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The dots given in the grid are the centres of rotationally symmetric “galaxies” (non-overlapping sets of orthogonally connected cells). Adjacent digits in the same galaxy must have a difference of at least 5. Caged cells are part of a galaxy with a given centre.

description:

https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2cokazj3 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along thermometers must increase from bulb to tip. (5:30/10:00)

GAS 754 – June 30, 2023: June 30, 2023 by Philip Newman https://tinyurl.com/yz5zuu2n 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2chz6qz9
Normal sudoku rules apply. Gray regions are clones and must contain the same digits in the same relative positions. (9:00/18:00)

GAS 755 – Renban Walls by clover  https://tinyurl.com/4wybsbmr 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=25tebn7h
Normal sudoku rules apply. For each of the vertical purple lines (‘renban walls’), the following are true: 
• The cells touching one side of the wall contain a set of consecutive digits, in any order.
• The cells touching the other side of the wall also contain a set of consecutive digits, in any order.
• When taken together, all the cells touching the wall contain a set of consecutive digits, in any order.

title: Holy Interactions, Batman!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
This might be the longest ruleset we've ever seen for a puzzle but, when that puzzle is by zetamath, exceptions have to be made!  This is an absolutely gorgeous sudoku with a string of beautiful logical deductions from start to finish.  Enjoy!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/9R8DNm8dq6

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each circle marks the head of a familiar line constraint which takes the form of a snake of length from 2 – 9 cells. The specific constraint is indicated by the colour of the circle (and by a letter on the colourblind friendly version). The circle contains the length of the snake. The snakes move orthogonally through the centres of some cells, and do not touch themselves orthogonally. Snakes may freely touch each other, but do not share cells. The grey cells in box 4 are not part of any snake. 

The featured clue types are as follows: 
Renban (purple/R): The digits on a renban line form a sequence of consecutive digits in any order. Digits do not repeat along a renban; 
Region Sum Lines (Blue/ S): The cells along a region sum line in each 3x3 box it passes through sum to the same total. Region sum lines always occupy at least two regions; 
German Whispers (Green/W): Adjacent digits along a German whispers line differ by at least 5; 
Modular Lines (Yellow/M): Each string of three adjacent cells along a modular line contains one of 147, one of 258, and one of 369. Length two modular lines contain one of each of two of these groups; 
Entropic Lines (Orange/E): Each string of three adjacent cells along an entropic line contains one of 123, one of 456, and one of 789. Length two entropic lines contain one of each of two of these groups; 
Parity Lines (Red/P): Adjacent digits along a parity line have opposite parity; 
Ten Lines (Gray/T): Digits along a ten line must be entirely divided into non-overlapping groups of adjacent cells which sum to 10. Digits may repeat within these sums if allowed by other rules.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We haven't solved an apiyo sudoku on the channel for too long and we get to put that right today with Phog Of War - a much recommended Fog Of War puzzle!

As one might expect, this is really very original and clever - see if you can work out how to start without cheating!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/Hq7FFftdtJ

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from that digit’s surrounding cells. No domino in the grid sums to 3. The perimeter cells of the grid sum to 172. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. Cells separated by a black dot must contain digits in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit is double the other). Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It's rare nowadays to find a puzzle with a simple ruleset that attracts such fantastic plaudits but Fanfare by James Sinclair is such a sudoku.  This isn't a Genuinely Approachable Sudoku but it's not THAT much harder than one and has some very interesting logic. 
  
Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/N4LJbJP3TR

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Digits in cells separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits in cells separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit is double the other).

description:
Here are the URLs for today's 5 GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles. Hat times are given as (two hats/one hat). Any correct solution gets you a dinosaur. 

GAS 746 – Consec. Pairs by clover https://tinyurl.com/4dvdt5fj 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2kfnvwrm
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cells joined by a white dot are consecutive. Not all dots are necessarily given. (6:00/11:00)

GAS 747 – You’ve Got a Friend In Me by Bill Murphy https://tinyurl.com/46etdsvv 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2ofo4h7n
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in green cells must be equal to either the box, row or column they are in.  (8:00/13:30)

GAS 748 – Inside Philip’s House by Philip Newman https://tinyurl.com/34t2sb69 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2hoovz9f
Normal sudoku rules apply. Slow Thermo: Digits along thermometers must not decrease (but can stay the same) from bulb to tip. (5:00/11:00)

GAS 749 – Two Sudokus by clover https://tinyurl.com/25bcx4yu 
(no f-puzzles link)
Place the digits 1-6 in each row, column, and 2x3 box of each overlapping 6x6 grid (one outlined in blue, one in black). And that’s it! (4:30/8:00)

GAS 750 – Count Different Sudoku by Bill Murphy  https://tinyurl.com/4pcmnfzf 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2bmanh8f
Normal sudoku rules apply. The small number in a two-cell cage indicates how many different digits surround the cage. Up to 10 cells touching the cage by a side or by a corner should be inspected. (7:30/13:00)

title: The Sudoku With Only Three Given 7s
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We continue to work through some older puzzles that really should have been showcased before but we somehow overlooked.  Today we try 7 Loop by the constructor Innocuous and it's mind-blowing.  The ruleset is remarkably simple but the logic... WOW!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/n8gt4Hgprp

Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits sum to the small clue in the corner. Draw a single closed loop of cells that moves from cell to cell orthogonally and passes through the 8 outer boxes of the grid (and may or may not enter the central 3x3 box). title: Don't CHEAT To Solve This Puzzle!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Scojo makes his debut today with an absolutely delightful twist on Fog Of War sudoku - this one features lines the nature of which need to be deduced!  You know how much we enjoy Fog Of War puzzles but this is a REALLY good fresh twist on the form.  You'll want to try this one! 

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/jpGbTb7jBF

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Placing a correct digit in the grid will clear any fog in the surrounding cells. Lines are Renbans, German Whispers, or Region Sum Lines. The identity of each line must be deduced. Lines never cross or branch in this puzzle. Therefore, if two line segments enter the same cell, those line segments must be connected. Renbans are a sequence of non-repeating digits in any order. Along German Whispers adjacent digits on the line have a difference of at least 5. Region Sum Lines have the same sum in every 3x3 box they visit. If a Region Sum Line visits a box multiple times, each visit is counted as a separate sum. A dot between two digits means that those digits are either consecutive or have a 1:2 ratio. Not all dots are given.

title: The Naughty Brain
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A new fillomino variant today courtesy of the innovative and brilliant Math Pesto!  It's called Bridges and Fillings but it's a lot less painful than going to the dentist.  Definitely an opportunity to solve this one more quickly than the video today; sometimes your brain is naughty and doesn't see things clearly!! Just put your parity hats on and get cracking :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/PB7BG3N9Jr

Rules: 
Divide the grid into polyominoes so that polyominoes of the same size (ie with the same number of cells) don't share an edge. Each cell contains a number equal to its polyomino's size. For each line, one circle contains an odd number, and the other an even. The odd circle gives the amount of odd numbers on the line (excluding itself), while the even circle gives the amount of even numbers (excluding itself). If an odd number is in a cell with an arrow, it gives the amount of odd numbers in that direction (excluding itself) and if the number is even, it gives the amount of even numbers (excluding itself).

title: Dominoes Meets Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A 100% rated sudoku today from the constructor Blobz - it's called Domino Trails 3 and combines Cave/Corral logic with sudoku (and dominoes!) This is a fascinating puzzle and extremely fun to solve. Give it a go if you can!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/QtHJR7mqh9

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells (the “hedges”) such that the unshaded cells (the “trails”) form an orthogonally connected area (with no loops) where no 2x2 group of cells is either fully shaded or unshaded. Different parts of the trail may touch diagonally (so checkerboard patterns ARE allowed). Note that hedges do not need to connect to the edge of the grid. The trails are completely tiled with non-overlapping dominoes. Caged cells are always trail cells and indicate two things: (a) the digit placed in the cage shows how many trail cells (including itself) can be seen orthogonally from that position (where hedges obstruct the view); (b) the small clue in the corner of the cage shows the total sum of the corresponding domino. Not all dominoes are marked with a cage.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A new and predictably exceptional sudoku today from zetamath titled Duplicity (because it has two of each type of clue it uses!)  As usual, his dazzling mind has made a quite beautiful puzzle and, as one solver put it, you just need to ask the right weird questions :)

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/t3tR9bGgjG

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  A purple line must contain a set of non-repeating consecutive digits (which can appear in any order). Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. Cells separated by a black dot must contain digits in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit must be double the other). In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow’s (grey) circle. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end. A digit in a black circle must appear in at least one of the four cells surrounding that circle. Digits along a blue line have an equal sum within each 3x3 box the line passes through. title: A Stunning New Sudoku Rule Combo
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Icing Disaster is a new puzzle by dumediat that combines two rulesets we're very familiar with: Region Sum Lines and X Sums.  The result is fairly mind-blowing and makes you think in totally new ways.  Seriously clever stuff!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://tinyurl.com/4w5w9veu

If you have trouble with tinyurl links then try this version:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/9Jhfjg6FbL

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a blue line must have an equal sum within each 3x3 box that line passes through, regardless of how many times the line exits and re-enters a region. The area outside the grid is considered one region for purposes of this rule. Different lines may have different sums. Numbers outside the grid give the sum of the first N digits in their respective row or column, where N is the digit nearest the clue (inside the grid). Eg The following statements describe how these lines must be interpreted (rows/columns 0 and 10 indicate cells outside the 9x9 grid): Box 1: r0c1 + r1c0 = r1c2 + r1c3 + r2c1 + r3c1 + r3c2 & Box 7: r8c0 + r10c3 = r7c1 + r8c1 + r9c1 + r9c2\n

title: We Asked For Beautiful And We Got It!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
In the video for yesterday's fantastic puzzle by Florian Wortmann we mentioned that the easiest way to have your puzzle featured on the channel was to submit something beautiful and approachable. (Because we are inundated with beautiful and impossible!) Well Nordy took us at our word and submitted this Snake Egg puzzle overnight.  And we kept our word by trying it immediately!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/23BhrPf6Q9

Rules: 
Shade some cells to form an orthogonally-connected, 1-cell wide snake that does not branch, does not loop, and does not touch itself orthogonally—but may touch itself diagonally. One end of the snake is given as a white circle. The remaining non-snake cells form ten, distinct, orthogonally-connected areas—one each of sizes 1 to 10. Areas of different sizes do not touch orthogonally, but they may touch diagonally. Each number in the grid must be part of an area of that size. A '?' represents any number from 1 to 10. [To enable the software to check your solution, in each non-snake cell write the size of that region. Use "0" instead of 10 for the 10 region!].

description:
Here's where you can try the incredible Anti Ratio Miracle by Jobo: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/6QfQ4hB79q 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Any two orthogonally adjacent cells cannot contain digits in a 1:2, 1:3, 1:4 or 1:5 ratio. Every horizontal set of three orthogonally connected cells within any 3x3 box is a modular sequence (i.e. must contain one digit from [1 4 7], one digit from [2 5 8] and one digit from [3 6 9]). Every vertical set of three orthogonally connected cells within any 3x3 box is an entropic sequence (i.e. must contain one digit from [1 2 3], one digit from [4 5 6] and one digit from [7 8 9]). There are no 3's in a corner of the grid.

title: The Mad Miracle Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Mark makes Simon open this one live on camera.  It's an absolute beast.  Incredible looking, seemingly impossible to understand (unless you're a computer programmer!) but is it actually solvable? Try thoughtbyte's Friendly Indexing Miracle and see what you think!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/Pbh6rNGPdg

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A cell is "friendly" if it contains its row, column, or 3x3 box number. [Boxes are numbered in normal reading order ie top left (box 1) through to bottom right (box 9).) All friendly cells are column and row indexers, and they must index at least one cell other than themselves. Column indexing: friendly digits in column X indicate the column in which the digit X appears in that row. Row indexing: Friendly digits in row X indicate the row in which the digit X appears in that column. Friendly indexer example: if r3c6 is a 2, then r3c2 is a 6 and r2c6 is a 3. Digits may not repeat along the indicated diagonal.

title: Understanding The Four Colour Theorem
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A heavily touted puzzle (not sudoku!) today in the form of Spectrum by MicroStudy.  This is one of the smoothest pencil puzzles we've seen - an absolute blast to solve and not monstrously hard.  Definitely one to have a go at if you can find a few minutes spare.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/GLjgtD4QDJ

Rules: 
Fillomino: Divide the grid into regions of orthogonally-connected cells such that no two regions of the same size (ie with the same number of cells) share an edge. Enter a number into each cell equal to the size of its region. Four Colour Theorem: Each region must be shaded entirely in one colour. There are a total of four different colours in the grid. Regions of the same colour cannot touch orthogonally. Additionally, regions of the same colour must be of different sizes. Arrows: Digits on arrows indicate the distance to the nearest cell of the same colour in the indicated direction (Adjacent cells are a distance of 1 from each other). Not all arrows are necessarily given.

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A very witty sudoku today by Wolff called Deuces Wild in which the dastardly digit 2 takes on nine different values!  This one is a lot of fun and will almost certainly make you think you've broken the puzzle a few times :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/RfjqGgLRht

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Adjacent numbers on the green line have a difference of at least five. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. Along a thermometer digits must increase from the bulb end. Black dots separate digits with a 2:1 ratio (ie one number is double the other). White dots separate consecutive digits. In cages digits sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits along a purple line form a set of consecutive integers without repeats. However, twos (2s) are wild! Ie For the purposes of any clue, a 2 can any value from 1 to 9 inclusive but each value may only be used once. Note that for cages, although digits may not repeat in a cage, their values may. A cage with a clue of 2 could consist of a 1 and a 2, with the wild 2 taking on the value of 1.

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We love Fog Of War puzzles - have we ever mentioned that?!  Today's is by James Sinclair and is called Fog, Deconstructed.  It's an 11x11 grid into which the 9x9 sudoku boxes need to be located and it's an absolute blast.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/p9TjBQfq8f

Rules: 
Fill the grid with nine non-overlapping 3x3 square regions, such that each region contains the digits 1-9 once each and no digit repeats in any row or column. Correctly entered digits clear the fog around them. Cells outside regions do not contain digits. Cages show the sum of their digits in the left-most cell of the highest row reached by the cage, and digits cannot repeat within a cage. Cells with a shaded square must contain an even digit. Cells with a shaded circle must contain an odd digit.

description:
*** NEW SUDOKU HUNT OUT TODAY ***
A sudoku hunt, Kraken The Cryptic (with a new movie theme!), was released this afternoon (1 July) at 4pm UK time on Patreon.  

Join us on Patreon for as little as $2 a month to play.

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Florian Wortmann returns to the channel today with a beautiful mishmash of sudoku, yin-yang and minesweeper!  It's got an all but perfect rating and is of average difficulty so do try and have a go at it if you have time :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/T3tMM749d7

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The black dot joins digits in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit is double the other). Not all dots are given. The sum of the digits along a grey line is equal to the sum of the digits in the circles at either end of the line. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area may be fully shaded or fully unshaded. The circles act as 'minesweeper' clues. Ie Cells containing a circle are always unshaded, and their value is the number of shaded cells in the surrounding 3x3 area (i.e. the up to eight cells that touch the circle either orthogonally or diagonally).

title: Cover Your Sudoku In Japanese Mats!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Two puzzles in one video today!  The first, by shye, is an example of the Japanese logic puzzle Tatamibari which Math Pesto has merged with sudoku in the second :)

Both puzzles are great but one is quite a lot harder than the other! 

Play the puzzles at the links below:

shye's tatamibari:
 https://tinyurl.com/393fs4vy

Rules:
Divide the grid into rectangular regions of orthogonally connected cells, each containing exactly one clue. A plus shaped clue means that the region it belongs to is a square. A line shaped clue means that the region it belongs to is a rectangle with the longer edge parallel to the line. Four regions may never share the same corner.

Math Pesto's Tatamidoku:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/pbb4pNb3T4

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by 5 or more. Divide the grid into non-overlapping rectangular regions so that each region contains exactly one small clue (found in the top left corner of some cells). Four regions cannot share the same cell corner. Digits may not repeat within a region and sum to that region's small clue. The digit placed in a small clue cell gives information about that region: 
1–4: The region has a greater width than height.
5: The region is a square. 
6–9: The region has a greater height than width.

title: The Great Zetamath Reef
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Zetamath and his partner Tristan have been busy moving house but, after a brief hiatus, he has returned to the sudoku world with a quite brilliant and devious puzzle called Reef.  This has a perfect 100% rating on Logic Masters, a wealth of plaudits and the dreaded 5* difficulty rating :)

(It is worth watching until the end of the video if you're worried about Simon's solve.)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/dhm2Md99Mt

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells in the grid.  Those cells are part of the "coral".  The rest of the cells are "water".  All coral cells are orthogonally connected.  All bodies of water connect to the edge of the grid.  No 2x2 is entirely water or entirely coral. Digits do not repeat within cages, and the sum of the coral cells within each cage must equal the sum of the water cells within that cage. The digit in a circle gives the number of cells within its cage which match its colour (coral or water).  The total includes itself.

Today we face the terrifying prospect of a sudoku dedicated to the great tormentor Gliperal!  It's called A Wonderful Discovery and it's by damasosos92.  It's hard to know how to describe this one - the geometric ideas are fascinating and fathomable but they probably aren't easy!

title: Doots and Don'ts!
description:

Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white Kropki dot must be consecutive. Digits separated by a black Kropki dot must have a ratio of 1:2. Not all Kropki dots are necessarily given. Sets of digits separated by a white Kroopki doot (the long, ellipse-looking things) must have their respective sums be consecutive. Sets of digits separated by a black Kroopki doot must have their respective sums be in a 1:2 ratio. Not all Kroopki doots are necessarily given. Digits along a blue line sum to the same total within each box that the line visits. Different lines may have different sums.

title: The Bishop takes his Chance
description:
Here's where you can play Contritum Quadratum by Pecha_berrie: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/JNL7j4DpP6 
Each row, column, and outlined region of the grid contains the digits 1–9 exactly once each. An 'X' between two cells means that that pair of cells must add to 10. a 'V' means the pair must add to 5 (INCLUDES negative constraint! All possible X's and V's are given). Within the gray 7x7 square in the grid, no digit can see another of itself diagonally (a 'bishop's move' in chess). For example, a 6 in r5c5 means that there cannot be a 6 in r3c7, but there may be one in r1c9, which is outside of the grid.

title: One Of The Best Debuts Ever
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A debut on the channel today for the constructor sophmayrob and their puzzle DIY Arrows.  If you spend a moment or two studying this one you may think it's quite approachable; if you spend another 5 minutes, you'll think it is absolutely impossible.  This is a seriously clever sudoku and one of the best debuts we've ever seen.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/tpjLQ6BhQ7

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a knight’s move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Cells separated by a grey dot contain digits that are either consecutive or in a 2:1 ratio. Standard arrow sudoku rules apply ie Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. In this puzzle the circles are given and the arrows must be found by the solver. Each arrow must be exactly 3 cells long (4 including the circle). Arrows can only extend into columns 123789 of the sudoku. Arrows can cross each other but may not share cells.

Draw a one-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells. The loop may not touch itself, not even diagonally. The loop must enter every cell of every cage. The loop acts as a German Whispers line (i.e., adjacent digits on the loop must have a difference of at least 5). Additionally the grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells, possibly revealing more clues.

title: What to do when your Brain goes down Dead Ends
description:
Here's where you can try Dead Ends by Trufflebear: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/4pgH6FFrmd 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along the thermometer, digits increase from the bulb end. The 'v' between two adjacent cells indicates that the cells sum to 5. The orange lines - three horizontal and five vertical - are sequences of digits with the property that successive digits must be at least 4 more or less than the previous digit. All sequences are to be read left to right, or top to bottom, as appropriate, and no two sequences are the same. Each sequence has the property that the final digit is a 'dead end' - that is, there are no valid digits that could follow it, were the line one cell longer. So for a five-cell line, 28194 would be valid as the 4 is a dead end (only an 8 or 9 can follow a 4), but 28193 would be invalid as a 7 could follow the 3.

title: Pac-Man: The Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Although we're normally quite careful about puzzles with long rulesets, we wanted to make an exception for this one from Math Pesto: Pac-Man Sudoku!  For many of us, this is a highly nostalgic theme and it's also a very entertaining sudoku puzzle (and not that easy!)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

With Pac-Man and ghost graphics:
https://tinyurl.com/mryew2rt

Normal link without graphics:
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/dLTrH6DM6F

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The leftmost and rightmost cells of a row are considered orthogonally adjacent for the purposes of ALL rules below. Cells joined by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Not all white dots are necessarily given. Shade some cells in the grid and leave the rest unshaded such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and no 2x2 region is entirely shaded. A cell containing Pac-Man, Blinky, Pinky, Inky, or Clyde (yellow, red, pink, blue, and orange)—or part of a white dot—must be shaded. A cell containing a small clue in the top-left corner is a “killer clue” and must remain unshaded. Digits may not repeat within an orthogonally connected area of unshaded cells, and they sum to the killer clue. (Note: Unshaded regions may not touch each other orthogonally and not all regions necessarily have a killer clue.) Starting in R5C2, Pac-Man must travel orthogonally through the grid. His path may not touch itself orthogonally, although it may do so diagonally, and the path cannot intersect or overlap itself. Pac-Man must go directly through each white dot; his path is completed immediately after going through the final dot. Pac-Man's path cannot be orthogonally adjacent to any of the ghosts (red, pink, blue, and orange) nor can the path enter unshaded cells.

*** NEW SUDOKU HUNT JUST OUT ***

title: What Happens when you get a Double Sandwich Sudoku?
description:
Here's where you can try Big Mac by Adem Jaziri: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/8NGMPRj4Dt 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage cannot repeat and must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. A clue outside the grid indicates the sum of the digits between X and Y, and also the sum of the digits between Y and Z in the corresponding row or column. X, Y and Z are the same for all the clues and must be determined by the solver. (For example, if X = 1, Y = 6 and Z = 9, the 7 clue indicates that the sum of the digits between 1 and 6 is equal to 7 and the sum of the digits between 6 and 9 is also equal to 7.) A '?' could represent any digit from 0 to 9. Different '?'s may represent different digits.

title: 144 Cells Of Logic
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The return of the brilliant constructor Agent today and a logic puzzle called Tunnel Vision.  This has a 100% rating on Logic Masters (so has not yet suffered from sabotage - see the video introduction) and it's seriously clever!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/4J83LHrpL4

Rules: 
Divide the grid into regions of orthogonally connected cells. Two regions of the same size may not share an edge. Enter a number into each cell equal to the size of its region (ie the number of cells in its region). Consider N the number in the top-left corner of a cell with arrows. Arrows indicate ALL the directions (up, down, left, and right) where the NEAREST occurrence(s) of N is/are located. The number placed in that cell indicates the distance to the first occurrence of N in the indicated direction(s).

title: Invisible Thermometers: A Game-Changing Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
So many of you have requested that we attempt this puzzle, Invisible Thermometers by Nahileon.  The ruleset seems completely ludicrous - who would come up with such a thing?!  Well it turns out that, yet again, Nahileon has produced something utterly mind-blowing.  But it is quite hard ;)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/frjRNFMDjB

Rules: 
Place the digits 1-8 once each in every row, column and region.  A digit in a cell with a circle must be odd. A digit in a cell with a square must be even.  There are invisible thermometers in this grid.  Every empty cell (the 6x6 in the center) gets visited by one of those thermometers.  Digits on a thermometer increase from the bulb on one end to the tip on the other end.  The thermometers are orthogonally connected and don't fork or overlap.  A thermometer may have length 1 if it's bulb and tip are the same cell.  The difference between bulb and tip must be unique for each thermometer.

*** NEW SUDOKU HUNT INCOMING TOMORROW ***
A new sudoku hunt, The Planets Suite, will be released tomorrow at 4pm UK time on Patreon.  It's one of our own and should be slightly easier this month. title: A Sudoku In The Danger Zone
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Lots of you have been asking about this puzzle - Highway To The Danger Zone by Jay Dyer.  It's definitely NOT easy but my goodness it's incredibly clever.  One of our longest ever sudoku solves (for which we apologise) but this magnificent creation is too good to miss.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/b3QH7jB4FJ

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.\n\nDivide the entire grid into killer cages, each of which is a set of orthogonally connected cells. Each cage contains exactly one clue, which may be in any position in the cage, and gives the sum of the digits in that cage. Digits may not repeat in a cage. Single cell cages are allowed.\n\nDraw a single loop through the centres of some cells with no branches or crossings, which visits each cage exactly once. The loop moves orthogonally from cell to cell. If two cells share an edge but are in different cages, at least one of them must be visited by the loop. The digit in a clued cell equals the number of cells in that cage which are visited by the loop.

https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2eyh3ane
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells which are diagonally adjacent cannot contain the same digit. (5:00/12:00)

title: Succession: Who Takes The Sudoku Crown?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
No Spoilers here but Simon is still reeling from watching the last ever episode of Succession last night.  So today we're going to tackle The Tilted Crown by fritzdis - an absolutely beautiful and unusual sudoku, which seems fitting given the Roy's battles for their own crown!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/ft3J69J2hG

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. 
Minimal between lines: Digits on a line must be between the digits in the connected circles.  The difference between the circled digits must be as small as allowed by normal sudoku rules.  For example, a circle in R1C2 connected with a straight line to a circle in R5C6 would have a difference of 2 because it is possible (and necessary) to repeat the same digit in all 3 spots along the line. 
Clones: The grey 4x4 regions must contain the same digits in the same arrangement. 
Skyscrapers: Each digit N in the grid represents a building of height N.  Numbers outside the grid indicate how many buildings can be seen from that direction in the row, with taller buildings blocking shorter buildings from being seen.

title: (Simply) the GAS
description:
Here are the URLs for today's 5 GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles. Hat times are given as (two hats/one hat). Any correct solution gets you a dinosaur. 

GAS 691 – Fortress by clover https://tinyurl.com/5duywcy3 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=26dszopw
Normal sudoku rules apply. Grey cells must be greater than all of the digits in orthogonally adjacent white cells. (7:00/13:00) 

GAS 692 – Determinant Sudoku by Bill Murphy https://tinyurl.com/5xxxctxm 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=247h2xz2
Normal sudoku rules apply. The determinants of 2x2 matrices are given in the center of four cells. The determinant of a 2x2 matrix is the product of one pair of diagonal cells minus the product of other pair, a*d-b*c, where a is the top left, b is the top right, c is the bottom left and d is the bottom right element. (7:30/14:00)

GAS 693 – Silent Green Is, People by Philip Newman https://tinyurl.com/227e6ckj 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2m82tdy7
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cells along a green line must differ by at least 5. (8:39/17:16)

GAS 694 Raspberry Lemon by clover! https://tinyurl.com/4b92mrtc 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2j6rccdp
Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits along each 'lemon' equals the two-digit number inside of that lemon, read from left to right. Each line also contains a set of consecutive digits, which can appear in any order. (8:00/15:00)

GAS 695 – Two Paintings by Nikolai Astrup by Bill Murphy https://tinyurl.com/5vz5sp89

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It is Bellal's birthday today and he and his son ThePedallingPianist have created the puzzle we attempt in tonight's video!  It's called Chromosomes.  It is a very challenging sudoku but features some absolutely mesmerising logic.

[Simon failed to click the tick at the end of the video - naughty Simon - but SPOILER ALERT his solution is correct.]

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/p8FLjRMMJ6

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on the blue line have an equal sum, N, within each 3x3 box through which it passes. For the purpose of the equal sums line, a digit in a 'doubler' cell counts as twice the digit's value. title: Join Me for a Round of 9
description:
Here's where you can try A round of 9 by Cornishjohn: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/9dhQD6bdfN  

Sudoku-style rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Find an orthogonally connected path of length 37 that does not touch itself, not even diagonally, starting in R1C1 and ending in R9C9. The path is split up into 9 sections, each of length 3,4 or 5. Each section starts with its own section number as the value of the first cell, starting with section 1 in R1C1. Each section ends with its own length as the value of the last cell. Yellow cells may not be on the path and give the number of cells surrounding itself (orthogonally and diagonally) that are on the path. All possible yellow cells are given. Blue cells may not be on the path. Not all blue cells are given.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
One of Simon's favourite Japanese logic puzzles is Heyawake and rockratzero has merged it with sudoku to create an absolutely first-class hybrid!  It's hard for us to know how difficult this one is as it will make a huge difference if you have some familiarity with Heyawake strategies but, even if you're a complete novice, this is a puzzle you won't want to miss!
  
Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/jgFjmHD7bb

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells in the grid. Shaded cells cannot share an edge with each other. The unshaded cells must form a single orthogonally-connected area. The digit contained in each circle indicates how many cells must be shaded in that 3x3 box. A contiguous line (vertical or horizontal) of unshaded cells cannot span two 3x3 region borders. The digits in a cage may not repeat and must sum to the value given in the top left of the cage. Shaded cells do not contribute to the total.

title: Wrogn Fogn !!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Possibly the greatest puzzle title ever.  James Sinclair combines two of our favourite things: Fog Of War and the Wrogn ruleset (in which all clues must be incorrect!).  This is as witty as a sudoku gets as well as being clever from start to finish.
  
Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://tinyurl.com/wrognfogn

If you cannot use tinyurl then this version should work:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/RRPttN2Dg2

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. All clues are standard, and all clues are wrong. A clue is 'wrong' if it is not 100% correct. Specifically:
 - Digits within a cage must not be a non-repeating set of digits that sum to the number in the corner (if given).
 - Digits on arrows must not sum to the number in the connected circle.
 - On thermometers, digits must not increase from the bulb to the tip.
 - Along green lines, at least one pair of adjacent digits must not differ by at least 5.
 - Along orange lines, at least one pair of adjacent digits must not differ by at least 4.
 - Large circles contain at least one digit which does not appear in the four surrounding cells.
 - Digits in cells with a shaded circle must not be odd.
 - Digits in cells separated by a V must not sum to 5.
 - Digits in cells separated by an X must not sum to 10.
 - Digits in cells separated by a small white dot must not be consecutive.
 - Digits in cells separated by a black dot must not have a 1:2 ratio.
 - Clues outside the grid must not give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal.
