description:
Here are the URLs for today's 5 GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles. Hat times are given as (two hats/one hat). Any correct solution gets you a dinosaur. 

GAS 681 – Succession by Philip Newman https://tinyurl.com/48zmtvd7 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=24dkhox4
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a (chess) king's move cannot contain the same digit. Digits in cells joined by a white dot are consecutive; digits in cells joined by a black dot are in a 2:1 ratio. (8:00/20:00) 

GAS 682 – Odd Tapa Sudoku by clover! https://tinyurl.com/yuyfbuf8 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2ymjyvgo
Normal sudoku rules apply. All odd digits form a single orthogonally connected group, and there are no 2x2 squares composed only of odd digits. (8:00/15:00)

GAS 683 – Wanna Be Starting Sumthing by Bill Murphy https://tinyurl.com/yejtp3m3 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=29vodcwp
Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of either the first and second or the second and third cells seen from the direction of that clue. For multiple clues the order of the clues must be determined. (8:30/16:00)

GAS 684 Cross Purposes by Philip Newman https://tinyurl.com/yckpc3p8 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=23ppfkpy
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cells along a green line must differ by at least 5. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the first X digits in the corresponding row or column, starting with the digit adjacent to the clue and continuing away from the clue, where X is the adjacent digit. (10:00/25:00)

GAS 685 – Entropic Lines by clover! https://tinyurl.com/2p94ur99 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2bg3z3vw

title: The Schrödinger Ruleset
description:
Apologies for the hiccup this evening.  The 8.30pm version of the video included 2 minutes of empty chair when Simon got called away.  The algorithm may punish this video now, which is a travesty because Nordy's puzzle is really quite amazing.  If you do enjoy it, please do "Like" it or even subscribe and help convince YouTube of what we already know :)

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Today's sudoku is called Wormholes (Remix) and it's from Nordy.  It boasts one of the strangest rulesets we've ever seen in that, even though the basis idea is very simple, it looks very complicated when written down. So it's alive and dead at the same time/easy and hard at the same time...   What's more this puzzle is incredibly clever in surprising ways.  Try and make time to give it a go!
  
Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/rT277BN3dF

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Numbers in the corner of cages indicate the number of cells in that 3x3 Box that form "wormholes" with other boxes. A cell in a cage in Box A forms a wormhole with the central cell of Box B when the cell's position in Box A (eg top right cell) matches the position of Box B in the grid (eg top right box). Two cells in a wormhole relationship both contain the same digit. Note: Cage totals only count the number of wormholes that look out of that box and into the central cells of other boxes ie A wormhole from another box that looks into the central cell of a cage is not counted.

title: Simon & Mark Solve Sudoku Together!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We wanted to say thank you to DiMono for his May Patreon reward and he suggested we might like to tackle one of his "beast level" puzzles... so today both Simon & Mark take on Everything Is Rihgt, an astonishing construction that must be solved twice; once with the clues treated as being true and once with the clues being treated as false!
  
Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/jq4RbMd67t

Rules: 
This is a puzzle that must be solved twice! Normal sudoku rules apply. Normal Killer, Little Killer, Quadruple, Kropki, Thermometer, Palindrome, Maximum, Minimum, and XV rules apply (see below for detailed rules). Red clues are each at least one of normal Skyscrapers, X-Sum, or Sandwich clues. After solving the puzzle, save your solution, because it's time to solve it again as a Wrogn puzzle! All clues in the grid must be made invalid in the finished solution, and red clues cannot be ANY of valid Skyscrapers, X-Sum, or Sandwich clues. To be considered invalid, the maximum cell must be less than AT LEAST one adjacent cell, the minimum cell must be greater than AT LEAST one adjacent cell, thermometers must NOT increase from bulb to tip, and quadruple circles may have some BUT NOT ALL listed digits in the surrounding cells. A "less than" sign effectively becomes a greater-than-or-equal-to sign. A "greater than" sign effectively becomes a less-than-or-equal-to sign. ADDITIONALLY, when solving the Wrogn version, no digit may be the same as it was in the Right version. i.e. if R1C1 was a 1 the first time, it may not be a 1 the second time. IT IS IMPOSSIBLE TO SOLVE THE WROGN VERSION WITHOUT FIRST SOLVING IT NORMALLY

Correct rules would be:
Killer: Digits cannot repeat within a cage and sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (if given).
Little Killer: Clues outside the grid with an arrow give the sum of the digits in the direction of the arrow.
Quadruple: The digit(s) in a circle must appear at least once in the four cells touching the circle.
Kropki: Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits; cells separated by a black dot must contain digits in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit must be double the other).
Thermometer: Along a thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb end.
Palindrome (grey lines without bulbs): digits along the palindrome must read the same forwards and backwards.
In a grey cell with four arrows facing outwards, the digit in the cell must be greater than the digits in the four orthogonally neighbouring cells.
In a grey cell with four arrows facing inwards, the digit in the cell must be less than the digits in the four orthogonally neighbouring cells.
XV: Cells separated by an X must contain digits summing to 10.
Sandwich: The clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits sandwiched between the 1 and 9 in that row/column.
X-Sums: The clue outside the grid gives the sum of the first X digits in that row/column, where X is the digit in the cell at the start of that row/column.
Skyscrapers: The clue outside the grid gives the number of buildings "seen" from the direction of the clue (treating each digit as a building with a size equal to its value and noting that taller (higher) digits therefore obstruct the view of shorter (smaller) digits.

description:
Here's where you can try to crack PreY by Fry: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/8BjhtTPtHM 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells joined by an X sum to 10. A marked diagonal has no repeat digits. Every cell on the marked diagonals points orthogonally outwards in every direction at a distance of x, where x is equal to the digit in the cell. Cells stop pointing in their respective direction if they cross over a marked diagonal. (e.g. if r4c4 was a 3 it would only point to the cells r1c4 and r4c1). Every 5 is being pointed at.

title: A (Sling)Shot In The Dark
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
So many of you enjoyed A Walk In The Mist a few days ago that we thought another Fog Of War sudoku might be a good idea.  So here is mnasti2's A (Sling)Shot In The Dark, which is a wonderful introduction to the "slingshot" ruleset!
  
Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/GThfJTPqtL

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit on a bent arrow shows how many cells away the digit in the cell from which the arrow originates appears in the direction of the arrow, e.g. if R1C4 was a 3, then whichever digit is in R2C4 would also be in R1C1. Under the fog, a double-headed arrow is two overlapping slingshots, and adjacent digits along a green line differ by at least 5.\n

title: The Yin and Yang of a Brilliant Hybrid Sudoku Puzzle
description:
Here's where you can try YYSL Knights by Blobz: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/2QrQPp6qPp 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected and no 2x2 area may be fully shaded or unshaded. White dots lie on the border between the shaded and unshaded regions. Additionally, white dots separate consecutive digits. Not all possible dots are shown. Digits in caged cells show the number of cells of the same color (shaded or unshaded) seen orthogonally from that position, including itself. The 'other' color blocks vision. Cells a (chess) knight's move apart cannot contain the same digit.

title: If You Watch One Video This Month...
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A simply incredible puzzle tonight from Piatato called Coordinate Arrows.  How we missed this when it came out in February 2022 we don't know but we get to put that right now and showcase a sudoku that is surely one of the best we've EVER seen.
  
Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/bNjqp79Rpn

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. (ie Every row, column, and 3x3 box must contain the digits 1-9 with no repeats.) Digits on an arrow spell out the coordinates for the digit that is their sum. The row number is written on the start of the arrow, the column number is written on the arrow tip. If, for example, an arrow looks like this: (14) then there must be a 5 in r1c4. All the arrows must correspond to different coordinates. Digits may repeat on an arrow if allowed by other rules.

title: Here come the GAS Gremlins
description:
Here are the URLs for today's 5 GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles. Hat times are given as (two hats/one hat). Any correct solution gets you a dinosaur. 

GAS 676 – Position Sums by clover! https://tinyurl.com/yzbdsvxc 
(no f-puzzles for this one)
Normal sudoku rules apply. The topmost two digits in each column, or the leftmost two digits in each row, are "A" and "B". The clues immediately adjacent to the grid tell you the sum of A+B (that is, the sum of the closest two digits) in some rows or columns. For the clues slightly further away from the grid, take the sum of the "Ath" and "Bth" digits in that row or column, counting left to right or top to bottom.  (8:30/15:00) 

GAS 677 – Home Maker by Bill Murphy! https://tinyurl.com/29st98fz 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=28vodhf6
Normal sudoku rules apply. And that’s it! (5:30/11:00)

GAS 678 – Squaring the Circles by Philip Newman https://tinyurl.com/y6yxkxx4 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=25sucxlz
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in grey cells must be greater than digits in orthogonally adjacent white cells. Digits in corner circles must appear in the surrounding four cells, in some order.  (8:00/16:00)

GAS 679 – Killer Sudoku by clover! https://tinyurl.com/43mc486z 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2334a38j

title: The Sudoku Revolution Is HERE
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Recently we've seen innovations galore in the world of sudoku with fog of war, sokoban and rush hour puzzles.  Now Malrog (with yet more help from Chameleon's programming skills!) brings us Revolutionary - a sudoku in which the clues can actually rotate.  This is absolutely brilliant.  
  
Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://tinyurl.com/2hv3n33v

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on an arrow sum to the value in the attached circle. Digits in a cage may not repeat and sum to the total given. Purple dots are pivot points for constraint clues, which rotate clockwise around their pivot point through N steps of 90 degrees, where N is the value on the pivot. Rotated clues may overlap but must not extend outside the grid.

Check Out The Number Of Solves For A Walk In The Mist here:

title: Only ONE Person Has Solved This Puzzle...
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Simon attempted this sudoku by Darth Paradox called Renrenbanban without much hope.  Only one person is known to have solved it on Logic Masters Germany and our testers couldn't do it.  But the ruleset was intriguing so he gave it a go...
  
Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/J74NR4224q

Rules: 
Place the digits 1-9 once into each row, column, and 3x3 box.  Digits must not repeat along the marked diagonal.  The grey lines are palindromes and must contain the same sequence of digits in both directions along the line. The purple lines are Double Renban lines.  Each such line contains two equal-sized sets of consecutive digits.  The sets might overlap partially or completely, and the digits can be in any order along the line.  For example, 123123, 172839, and 142332 are each valid ways to fill a six-cell Double Renban line.

title: Rush Hour Sudoku: The 9x9 Version!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A couple of weeks ago we were amazed by Chameleon's implementation of a 6x6 Rush Hour themed sudoku in which the cars could be moved around the grid carrying given digits around with them.  Well rockratzero has managed to create a 9x9 version called Reserved Parking.  It is difficult to imagine a more innovative ruleset!!
  
Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://yusitnikov.github.io/puzzletv/#reserved-parking

One tip: When you finish the puzzle, make sure to enter a full size digit over each black digit in the grid to allow the software to check your solution properly!

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Rush Hour mechanics apply to car movements; given digits on cars move with the cars. Digits on pink lines and pink cars must form a set of consecutive numbers in any order. Adjacent digits on green lines and green cars must vary by at least 5. Digits adjacent on black dots and black cars must form a 2:1 ratio. Cars may not permanently park adjacent/touching a black dot. (Example: in row 6 starting positions, the black car is touching, but the pink car is not). Initially no cars may leave the caged 6x6 Region. Move the Red Car through the Cage opening and into the red outlined Parking Space to allow the other cars to move outside this initial cage. (Press the button that appears to release the cars.) Other cages in the grid are Reserved Parking spaces. Park the correspondingly coloured cars in their space. Reserved Parking have hidden given digits to be discovered while driving. Revealed digits do not move.

title: What Is "Schreedinger's" Cat?!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Mark is up to his usual tricks today by getting Simon to open Schreedinger's Cat live on camera.  This sudoku, from Christounet, features cells that must contain not one, not two but THREE digits.  And this messes up one's head!!!
  
Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/tT7m9JG8Nd

Rules: 
Normalish sudoku rules apply : Put the digits 0-9 into each row column and box once each. In order to allow this, each row, column, and box will have one "Schreedinger-cell" which contains exactly 3 digits. The value of any "Schreedinger-cell" is the sum of its 3 digits. This will affect the arithmetic on arrows, renbans, german whispers and kropki dots. Arrows: the values of cells along an arrow sum to the value in that arrow's circle. Renban: the values of cells on a renban (purple) line form a set of non-repeating consecutive numbers in any order. German Whispers: the values of cells along a green line must differ by at least 5. Quadruples: the digits contained in the small white circles must each appear at least once in the 4 surrounding cells. Kropki: black dots separate cells whose values have a 1:2 ratio. Note that two of the renbans and two of the german whispers lines join cells that are a "chess knight's move" apart. For example, R6C1 and R5C3 must differ by at least 5.

*** NEW SUDOKU HUNT NOVEL BY DIMONO JUST OUT ***
A new sudoku hunt wrapped in a real novella has just been released as our May monthly reward on Patreon.  It's by DiMono and you need to keep solving puzzles to access the later chapters of the story!

title: The 11x11 Emperor
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
On Star Wars Day, it seems appropriate that Simon take on a true Emperor of a puzzle.  Jay Dyer's Overlarge is one of the most challenging sudokus we've ever seen but boy is it BRILLIANT!
  
Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/RmmfTLFJqB

Rules: 
Contained within the grid are nine non-overlapping 3x3 regions, which must be located. Each region contains the digits 1-9 once each, so that no digit repeats in any row or column. Cells outside regions don't contain digits. Each region contains a single "doubler" cell, whose value is double its digit for the purpose of cage totals. No row or column contains more than one doubler, and each digit appears in exactly one doubler. Digits may not repeat in a cage, and the sum of cell values in a cage equals the clue in the top left corner of the cage.

title: Which Line Is It Anyway?!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A fabulous idea for a puzzle today as Marty Sears asks us Which Line Is It Anyway? Allocate a rule to a line and solve the sudoku - sounds simple but actually it's very interesting :)
  
Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/GLtpHJ9MhF

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each of the seven line types listed below appears once in the grid. You must determine which line is which. RENBAN LINE: Contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits, in any order. GERMAN WHISPER LINE: Adjacent digits along the line have a difference of at least 5. THERMOMETER: Digits are arranged in ascending order, from one end to the other, without repeats. REGION SUM LINE: Along the line, digits within each 3x3 box have the same total. The line visits at least two different boxes. PALINDROME LINE: The sequence of digits along the line reads the same in either direction. PARITY LINE: All digits on the line have the same parity. UNLUCKY LINE: Adjacent digits along the line sum to at least 13.

Rules: 
Break the grid entirely into "ominos" ie orthogonally-connected regions of some size.  Each omino contains a digit equal to the size of its omino (in number of cells), and two ominos of the same size may not touch orthogonally (but may touch diagonally). Draw a loop that moves orthogonally through the centres of some cells.  The loop must visit each omino exactly once, but may visit any number of cells within that omino from one up to the full size of the omino.  If two orthogonally adjacent cells are both unvisited by the loop, there cannot be a border between them. The grid line pointed at by an arrow acts as a border between ominos.  The number in the target cell (ie the cell the arrow points to) gives the number of cells within the omino containing the arrow that are visited by the loop.

description:
Here's where you can try Nothing's Perfect by NotThatItMatters: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/D439327Fp9 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Within each row, column and box is one 'marker' cell. Marker cells must contain all digits EXCEPT 6. The row for each marker cell is indicated in row 1 of the grid. For example, if r1c2 = 9 then r9c2 is a marker. The column for each marker cell is indicated in column 1 of the grid. For example, if r3c1 = 7 then r3c7 is a marker. The position for each marker cell within a box is indicated in the lower-right corner of the box (position 9). For example, if r3c3 (lower-right for box 1) = 2, then r1c2 is a marker. Black Kropki dots in the grid indicate adjacent cells in the ratio of 2:1 (one cell is twice the other). ALL black dots are shown.

title: One Of The Best Puzzles We've Ever Seen
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Yesterday we showcased a puzzle which had somehow "only" got a 99% rating.  Today we go further:  Cross The Sums by abed hawila has a mere 97% BUT this is one of the best puzzles we've EVER seen. A complete joy from start to finish.
  
Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/hf4GBqrgDJ

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells so that the outside clues indicate the sums of the contiguous shaded cells in that row or column. A number indicates the sum of a complete contiguous block. A question mark (?) indicates that a contiguous block sum to a single-digit number and a double question mark (??) indicates that a contiguous block sums to a double-digit number. An asterisk implies that any number of blocks may exist, including zero. The clues are provided in the correct order (left-to-right, or top-to-bottom), and there is at least one unshaded cell between each pair of clued blocks. The shaded cells form a single orthogonally connected group. No 2×2 area within the grid can be totally shaded.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An exceptional debut on the channel today for Bren77 and their puzzle Hot And Cold Cages, which introduces a ruleset we don't think we've seen before (although it feels familiar!).  This has a completely unjustified 99% approval rating on Logic Masters Germany - unjustified because how it's lost 1% we have literally no idea. This is wonderful!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/jPmjLqHfbp

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. In every row, column and 3x3 box there is exactly one "hot" cell (which has a value one greater than its digit) and exactly one "cold" cell (which has a value one less than its digit). description:
Here are the URLs for today's 5 GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles. Hat times are given as (two hats/one hat). Any correct solution gets you a dinosaur. 

GAS 656 – HI by Philip Newman https://tinyurl.com/4srh85vy 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2ffrabd7 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cells joined by a black dot must have a ratio of 2:1. Not all dots are necessarily given. (6:36/12:48) 

GAS 657 – Difference 2 Neighbor by clover! https://tinyurl.com/3z6sn5fx 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2ju4rdu7
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each digit in a gray cell must have at least one orthogonal neighbor that is exactly 2 more or 2 less than it. Not all gray cells are necessarily given. (7:00/13:00)

GAS 658 – Emitter Sudoku by Bill Murphy https://tinyurl.com/4mbna2cj 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2fdbsg78
Normal sudoku rules apply. Four lines of cells originate at each emitter (circled digit), one in each direction. Digits along each line must have a sum no greater than the value of the emitter itself; also, each line must be as long as possible (that is, if a line were longer by one cell, the sum would be greater than the emitter value). If no line is given in a direction, the adjacent cell is higher than the circled digit. (9:00/17:00)(special 2-hat time for Mark: 7:30)

title: The Best Thing To Happen To Sudoku This Year
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
In 2022, Chameleon came up with the Fog Of War mechanic - a completely innovative and brilliant new form of sudoku.  In 2023, Chameleon has done it again by creating Rush Hour Sudoku - in which the player must slide the tiles (cars!) to allow the sudoku to be logically solved.  This is ground-breaking and awesome fun.  Don't miss it!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://yusitnikov.github.io/puzzletv/#rush-hour

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply: place digits 1-6 into every row, column and 3x2 box, once each.
There are cars on the grid, and they carry given digits. The cars could be moved forward and backward in their direction, but they cannot drive through another car or through the grid border (they cannot escape from the grid). The given digits on the cars drive together with the car.
Software tips:
- Use the move button (4 arrows) for moving the cars.
- You can hide the cars by pressing the yellow car button.

title: The Identical Sudokus
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Some constructors exhibit a level of genius that it is just a privilege to behold.  Jay Dyer's Dimorphism breaks the mould with 2 linked 6x6 grids - that look almost identical.  But they will break your brain :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://tinyurl.com/mva8jjf5

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/dB4gb8FMNL

Rules: 
In each grid, place the digits 1-6 in cells such that each row/column/region contains all digits once each. Each grid contains six 'sum cells', one per row/column/region. The value of a sum cell equals the cell's digit plus the digit in the same position in the other grid. No digit can appear in more than one sum cell in the same grid. Sum cells may be in the same position in the two grids. Along a red line, the cells' values form a non-repeating set of consecutive numbers in any order. Along a blue line, the sum of cell values is the same in each region the line passes through. White dots connect cells with consecutive values. Not all dots are necessarily given.

Here's where you can try Bloodcursed Arrows by ViKingPrime: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/h6Mddj29b8 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the value in its circle. There are 9 Vampire cells contained within the grid which are a set of the digits from 1-to-9. Each row, column and box contains exactly one Vampire cell. 9 Prey cells in the grid follow the same rules as the Vampire cells. A cell may have only one of these roles. For Arrows/Circles: Prey cells contribute no value; Vampire cells contribute the sum of the digits in the Vampire cell and the Prey cell within the same box.

title: A Sudoku With Only Four Given Lines
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
These lines might not be liars but they're certainly hiding the truth about their real natures in SSG's puzzle, Just Sum Ambiguity!  For those of you who enjoy a little arithmetical beauty in your sudokus this will be an absolute treat :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/NJgTqnNp9j

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. In addition, the sum of digits along a line must be the same within each 3x3 box the line passes through. eg r9c1+r9c2+r8c3 [line cells in box 7] = r9c4+r8c5 [line cells in box 8]. Furthermore, each line is either an Entropic Line or a Modular Line. Along an entropic line any run of three cells contains exactly one low {1,2,3}, one medium {4,5,6}, and one high {7,8,9} digit. Along a modular line, the digits in any run of three cells must all have different remainders under division by 3. (ie So one digit must be from the set {1,4,7}, one from {2,5,8} and one from {3,6,9}).

title: Short and Very Sweet
description:

Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a purple line form a set of consecutive digits in any order. Adjacent digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5. title: Using the Subway to Complete a Marathon?
description:
Here's where you can try Boston Marathon by FigoHarr: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/bbJb3DpG8M 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each of the colored lines represents one of the subway (the T) lines. Adjacent digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5; digits along the blue line have an equal sum N within each box it passes through; cells on an orange line form a consecutive nonrepeating set in any order; each digit on the red line must repeat once (ie appear twice on the line). Digits joined by a white Kropki dot must be consecutive. Digits joined by a black Kropki dot must have a ratio of 1:2. title: The 12 Degrees Of Separation
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An unusual and fascinating pencil puzzle today called Pentopia by au voleur! The idea is to fit pentominoes into the grid, without repeats and without them touching - oh and subject these odd arrow clues :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/BntmPfnd4L

Rules: 
Place pentominoes in the grid so that no pentominoes are in adjacent cells that share an edge or corner. Two pentominoes of the same shape cannot repeat in the grid; rotations and reflections of a pentomino are considered the same shape. The arrow clues indicate all the directions (up, down, left, and right) where the nearest pentominoes are located when looking from that square. (Pentominoes cannot sit on the cells with arrow clues.)

title: Zooming on a Sudoku Mission!
description:
Here's where you can try the FOUR puzzles involved in Zoom by Matyas Martinka – Layer 1: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/mFgHtTDMDg 
Place the numbers 1-3 exactly once in every row and column. Maximum cell: The value in the grey cell is higher than its four orthogonal neighbours. German Whispers: Adjacent digits along the marked lines have a difference of at least 2.
Keep the numbers that match their row number (1 from the first row, etc). Remove the rest of the digits and zoom out.
Layer 2: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/72ppFL88gM 
Place the numbers 1-5 exactly once in every row and column. Maximum cell rules still apply. German Whispers: Adjacent digits along the marked lines have a difference of at least 3. Kropki: The two cells connected by a dot contain consecutive numbers.
Keep the numbers that match their row number (1 from the first row, etc). Remove the rest of the digits and zoom out.
Layer 3: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/htgnqDD2hH 
Place the numbers 1-7 exactly once in every row and column. Maximum cell and kropki rules still apply. German Whispers: Adjacent digits along the marked lines have a difference of at least 4. Anti-king: The same digit cannot appear in diagonally adjacent cells.
Keep the numbers that match their row number (1 from the first row, etc). Remove the rest of the digits and zoom out.
9x9: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/LpPFjm9J7q 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Maximum cell, kropki and anti-king rules still apply. German Whispers: Adjacent digits along the marked lines have a difference of at least 5.

title: A Whisper Of The Divine
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

Today's sudoku has had some incredible praise from some of the world's best puzzle makers/solvers.  It's called Hopscotch (Remix), it's by Nordy and it is another example of the breathtaking beauty present in many of these new variant sudokus.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/Q3NL4tDB7p

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Every 3x3 box contains one hidden 2x2 region called a Whisper Square. In a Whisper Square, orthogonally adjacent digits must have a difference of 5 or greater. Whisper Squares must not touch each other orthogonally, but they may touch diagonally. Within each cage, the sum of digits inside Whisper Squares equals the sum of digits outside Whisper Squares.

title: The Perfect Miracle Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

Ever since May 2020 when we first released The Miracle Sudoku video, constructors have been searching for a "Perfect" Miracle Sudoku ie one where the entire sudoku grid was empty.  The only good examples we've seen still had very long rulesets but today we can share with you this new discovery from Farkov and TopAutism, An Easter Miracle.  That this puzzle exists is quite extraordinary.  Give it a try and see if you agree.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/3BqbqHQq3B

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Mark nine cells such that there is one marked cell in each row, column and 3x3 box. The digit in the first cell of a row, column, or 3x3 box gives the position of the marked cell in that row, column or 3x3 box. Each digit appears in exactly one marked cell. [Eg if r5c3 was a marked cell then r5c1 would be a 3 (marked cell is 3rd position in its row); r1c3 would be a 5 (marked cell is 5th position in its column); and r4c1 would be a 6 (marked cell is the 6th position in normal reading order of its 3x3 box).] Orthogonally adjacent digits may not be consecutive. In boxes 1, 2 and 3 each digit's position number within a box must equal that digit at least once.

title: The Most Terrifying Name In The Puzzle World Is...
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

Gliperal.  That is a puzzler's most terrifying name.

Today he returns to the channel with a puzzle themed around pentominoes.  It's ruined our testers and has very few solves on Logic Masters Germany.  Can Frodo (Simon) get to Mount Doom without Gliperal's eye spotting him?

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/9dR9Gtj6R8

Divide the grid into pentominoes, such that no two pentominoes of the same shape (including rotations and reflections) touch orthogonally. title: The Broken Secret
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A quite remarkable sudoku today from damasosos92 called Glyphs #5.  (Lara Croft makes no appearance in the puzzle!) This 100% rated 5* difficulty challenge is fascinating and baffling in equal measure! And why do none of those cages add up to the Secret?!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/bjD8gPPjqG

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a single line connecting 29 different cells in the grid that starts and ends with the two given digits. The line can reach a cell in the border of the grid only at the start or at the end of its path. The line cannot intersect itself and cannot branch. No 2x2 in the grid can be entirely covered by the line or entirely not-reached. Adjacent digits on the line must be consecutive. In cages, the digits on the line sum to the cage total.

title: The Puzzle Hidden In The Instagram Logo
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An absolutely amazing original sudoku today from Christounet - who wowed us a few weeks ago with a Back To The Future themed puzzle.  This one looks a bit like the Instagram logo!  It looks like there's a lot of thermometers to be used but how does one actually use them?!

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/mGLB4pqJt4

Normal sudoku deconstruction rules apply. ie Fill the grid with nine non-overlapping 3x3 square regions, such that each region contains the digits 1-9 once each and no digit repeats in any row or column. title: A Sudoku With No Visible Cells (!)
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Jay Dyer decides the best way to present a Fog Of War sudoku is with absolutely no cells visible!  Blackout, her latest puzzle, is weird and most definitely wonderful with some absolutely unique logic.  See if you can find your way through the fog (and don't cheat!)  

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/h9q22bptmF

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells are initially covered in fog, and placing correct digits will clear the fog around those digits. Mark nine cells such that there is one marked cell in each row, column and 3x3 box. The digit in the first cell of a row, column or 3x3 box gives the position of the marked cell in that row, column or 3x3 box. Each digit appears in exactly one marked cell. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5.\n\nEg if r5c3 was a marked cell then r5c1 would be a 3 (marked cell is 3rd position in its row); r1c3 would be a 5 (marked cell is 5th position in its column); and r4c1 would be a 6 (marked cell is the 6th position in normal reading order of its 3x3 box).

title: And Then There Were None by Agatha "fjam" Christie
description:
*** NEW SUDOKU HUNT TODAY ***
A new sudoku hunt, Knightmare On Sudoku Street, was released today at 4pm UK time on Patreon.  It features 19 puzzles by the Sudoku Skunkworks.  

Joining us on Patreon costs as little as $2 a month.  

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
WARNING.  Today's puzzle was sent to Simon (by Mark, who else!) as an April Fool.  It is exceptionally unusual for us to showcase a sudoku that requires "lateral thinking" to be solved, not just cold hard logic. It's called And Then There Were None and it's the work of fjam, who has recreated Agatha Christie's original murder mystery complete with poem.  It's a staggering (and incredibly challenging) affair AND you'll need to know about a lot of sudoku variant rules to even have a chance of solving it.  

As a one-off, we hope you'll agree that this is a spectacular way to celebrate April Fools Day!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/mJ84P77h6g

Rules: 
Detective, after bad weather we have finally been able reach the island following the distress call. Though we are yet to identify each victim, it appears that all ten digits died in accordance with the following verse:

Ten little digits sat down to dine; One was evenly spread in a sandwich and then there were nine.
Nine little digits under white cliffs slept late; One was crushed by stones and then there were eight.
Eight little digits heard whispers of heaven; One collapsed in the crossing and then there were seven.
Seven little digits cut up renban sticks; One chopped itself symmetrically and then there were six.
Six little digits played with bows and knives; An arrow tip pierced one and then there were five.
Five little digits were tried under law; One was shot for different parity and then there were four.
Four little digits took a trip out to sea; A red herring swallowed one and then there were three.
Three little digits got stuck together with glue; One was squashed between the others and then there were two.
Two little digits lay under the sun; One melted at peak temperature and then there was one.
One little digit with nowhere to run; Oddly still killed and then there were none.
We have also found a note, where one unidentified digit confesses to the murder of the other nine. We believe you should be able to solve the mystery by filling in the grid legitimately with the nine victims, leaving out the murderer. A few extra details from the note: Normal sudoku variant rules apply. Sandwich crusts have been marked with thin rectangles and contain the highest and lowest digits in the grid. Each line of the rhyme refers only to the remaining digits. Some victims have been identified by cages in the grid.

Standard sudoku variant rules include:

 - purple lines must contain consecutive digits
 - adjacent digits on green lines must differ by at least 5
 - along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end
  - digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle
 - digits along a line between two circles must have values between those in the circled ends
 - cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits.

Happy Birthday No-Feet McGee who turns 30 today and we celebrate by attempting their Build Your Own Arrow Sudoku puzzle.  This is just really clever with some surprising and lovely logic throughout.  Give yourself a treat and have a go!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/rbBB4tF8HL

Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. However, only the tip of each arrow is shown; the rest of the arrow (including the circle) must be determined by the solver. Arrows may only move orthogonally, not diagonally, and may not overlap. title: The Sudoku Grid Is ALL Fog??!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We celebrate Missing A Few Cards' birthday today but trying another of their collaborations with Full Deck called I'll Cry If I Want To.  And this puzzle might actually make you cry - it's a 'fog of war' sudoku with no cells revealed at all.  Mark tested it and said it was VERY hard.  Simon attempts it in a video and can confirm this assessment... but it's also as clever as you'd expect from two eminent math professors!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/N9TnrTD43m

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along modular lines, every set of three contiguous digits has three different remainders when divided by 3. Numbers outside the grid give the sum of the first X digits (the "X-Sum") along that row or column, where X is the first digit seen from the direction of the clue. In addition to any modular lines revealed as the fog lifts, every X-sum forms a hidden straight modular line at least X cells long starting from the cell closest to the clue. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. ALL blacks dots are given. As correct digits are placed, fog will lift, potentially revealing more clues.

title: A Real Battle with the GAS
description:
Here are the URLs for today's 5 GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles. Hat times are given as (two hats/one hat). Any correct solution gets you a dinosaur. 

GAS 626 – Boa by Philip Newman https://tinyurl.com/bdcwj8py 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2q97afal
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages must not repeat and must sum to the total given. (6:30/13:00) 

GAS 627 – Battleship Sums Sudoku by clover! https://tinyurl.com/2duj274x 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Place the eight given length-3 ships into the grid so that no ships touch each other, not even diagonally. (Ships can be horizontal or vertical). Some ship segments are already provided. Clues adjacent to a row or column tell you the sum of all digits on ship segments in that row or column. (Digits only – not shading – are required for answer check.) (11:00/20:00)

GAS 628 – The Goblin King by Bill Murphy https://tinyurl.com/3uckpzcd 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2jdzr2wj
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells connected diagonally cannot contain the same number. (7:30/15:00)

GAS 629 – Don’t Nock It by Philip Newman https://tinyurl.com/26cd5u3t 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2mka9sds
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along arrows must sum to the circled total. (Digits may repeat if allowed by other rules.) (8:00/15:00)

GAS 630 – Block Sum Relations by clover!  https://tinyurl.com/4ate22s7 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2j957etf
Normal sudoku rules apply. Equals signs in the grid tell you that the three digits above the clue have the same sum as the three digits below, or the three digits to the left of the clue have the same sum as the three digits to the right. For example, r2c1+r2c2+r2c3 = r2c4+r2c5+r2c6, and r4c8+r5c8+r6c8 = r7c8 + r8c8 + r9c8. (7:00/13:00)

title: Absolutely A-Maze-Thing!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Fjam has made a speciality out of these "find a path through the grid" puzzles and this is SUCH a great example of the form.  There's some really unusual and clever logic to be found from the modulo arithmetic - we think there could be more legs in this sort of sudoku!

Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/hr2j4L9gQg

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Navigate the maze by carefully plotting an orthogonally connected path from the green cell to the red cell. The path must include every cell containing an arrow, first entering the bulb and then travelling directly along the arrow. Every cell in the grid is associated with a cardinal direction (NESW), given by its digit modulo 4. The path must exit every cell it enters according to these directions. Which direction corresponds to which digits is to be discovered.

title: Juggling with Thermometers
description:
Happy birthday, Cora in France - I will mention this properly tomorrow!  Here's where you can play Temperature Inversion by Die Hard: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/qjhGjL3B3T 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on the marked diagonal must not repeat. Digits separated by a king’s move must not repeat. The grid contains a number of bidirectional thermometers (ie: digits must increase from the bulb end, but the bulb end is not known). Each thermometer contains either all odd or all even digits. The blue and red thermometers are special: Firstly, the position of their bulbs are known and are coloured. Secondly, the blue bulb is colder than the red bulb (ie: it contains a lower digit). Thirdly, the blue thermometer is colder than the red thermometer (ie: the sum of its digits is lower).

title: A Colourful Galactic Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We like sudokus that just have one puzzle in them but this one combines three!  You've got spiral galaxies, starbattle AND killer sudoku to do if you want to crack this one from AnalyticalNinja and Clocksmith - and all of the parts are clever and enjoyable.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/m7Grm47T9H

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The dots are the centres of rotationally symmetrical “galaxies” of orthogonally connected cells. (ie If you rotate the shape of the galaxy around 180 degrees you must get the same shape.) Each cell in the grid belongs to exactly one of these galaxies. Each row, column, and 3x3 box contains exactly 2 stars, and every galaxy contains exactly 1 star. Stars can't be within a kings move (in chess) from each other. Each galaxy with a small number clue in it sums to the number indicated. Digits can't repeat within a galaxy and “star” cells do not contribute to the totals shown.

title: A Game Of Tetris
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The current trend for creating hybrid puzzles combining sudoku with Japanese logic puzzles continues with this remarkable offering today: Sashigane Sudoku by Ambrose.  The rules seem a bit like Tetris to us and the solve is a complete delight.

Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/3n92Hf2fGQ

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into 1-cell wide L-shaped regions. Digits may not repeat in a region. A circle in a cell means that cell is the bend in a region, and also the number in that cell is how many cells are in that region (this rule does not apply to regions without a circle). An arrow in a cell means that cell is an end of a region, the arrow points to the bend, and also the value in the cell counts the number of cells in that leg of the region, including the bend cell (this rule does not apply to end-cells without arrows). A small clue in the top left corner of a cell gives the sum of the cells in that cell's region. Corner clues do not need to be in the top left cell of a region. A region may be lacking any or all clue types.

title: Quicksmart GAS
description:
Here are the URLs for today's 5 GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles. Hat times are given as (two hats/one hat). Any correct solution gets you a dinosaur. 

GAS 621 – Odd/Even/Big/Small by clover! https://tinyurl.com/mfymaz3w 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2fn6p9wk
Fill the grid with the digits 1-8 so that each row, column, and 2x4 region contains each digit exactly once. Letter clues outside of the grid tell you about the first two digits (closest to the clue) in their row/column, as follows. O = odd = 1/3/5/7 E = even = 2/4/6/8 S = small = 1/2/3/4 B = big = 5/6/7/8 (6:00/11:30) 

GAS 622 – Prime Sudoku by Bill Murphy https://tinyurl.com/4nrf33us 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2em35ack
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits connected by a black dot must sum to a prime number. (Relevant primes are 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17.) (7:30/13:30)

GAS 623 – Good Title by Philip Newman https://tinyurl.com/bdf5ftsj 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2nus9mb7
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along thermometers must strictly increase from bulb to tip. Digits in orthogonally adjacent cells (anywhere in the grid) cannot be consecutive (have a difference of 1). (6:42/13:57)

GAS 624 – Position Sudoku by clover https://tinyurl.com/5n74rhay 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2k48xsnf  
Normal sudoku rules apply Clues outside the grid tell you the relative position of the largest digit out of the three digits nearest that clue in that row/column. The position is counted inwards from the direction of the clue. (8:00/15:00)

GAS 625 – High Tea by Bill Murphy  https://tinyurl.com/26ubx8nr 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2mofsotk 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid give the sum of digits between 1 and 9 in that row or column.  (8:00/15:00)

title: Race Around The Grand Prix Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Happy Pi Day!  If you like Formulas, especially Formula 1, then give Grand Prix by Blobz a try - it's approachable, clever and above all great fun!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/J3mq7L7GrN

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages sum to the clue in the top left corner. Two race cars (blue and green) start in box 1 and race around the track to the chequered flag line in box 2 (in the 16 cage). Draw green and blue lines to show the paths that the cars take. Each checkpoint (cage) shows which cell each car passes through. The cars may not enter grey shaded cells, and must avoid all oil slicks (given digits). The paths cross exactly 3 times during the race. The paths do not share cells. Digits along the blue path have an equal sum N within each 3x3 box the path passes through.  Adjacent digits along the green path must differ by at least 5.

A debut on the channel today for the constructor Allagem and an absolutely beautiful sudoku called Eye of Agamotto - which just so happens to be perfectly rotationally symmetric.  What does this mean?  See if you can solve the puzzle to find out.

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/pjdTmP6JRt

Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. A digit in column 1 indicates the column in which the digit 1 appears in that row. title: Back To The Sudoku Future!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A debut on the channel today for Christounet and their magnificent homage to Back To The Future called Careful With That Hook, Emmett (a reference to Pink Floyd perhaps?).  This one features the dreaded Schrodinger Cells too which leads to some absolutely gorgeous logic.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://tinyurl.com/4s6dkx7z

If you cannot use tinyurl, here is an alternative link (with very slightly worse graphics but more complete rules!): 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/qh6TFtgTfd

Rules: 
Every row, column and 3x3 box contains the digits 0-9 once each. To enable this, one cell in each row, column, and 3x3 box is a Schrödinger cell (S-Cell) ie it contains two digits. The diagonal (marked in blue) must contain the digits 0 to 9 once each. Digits on a purple line form a set of non-repeating consecutive digits in any order. Digits along a grey arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. The sum of the digits in the two orange circles is equal to the sum of the digits along the orange line. Digits on the blue line have an equal sum N within each 3x3 box it passes through. Note that the blue line is partially hidden by the circle in R8C6. Digits in a cage sum to the clue in the cage's top left corner. The digits contained in the small white circles must each appear at least once in the 4 surrounding cells. Digits on the thermometer must increase from the bulb end. If an S-cell is on any arrow/arrow circle, cage or blue line, its value is the sum of the S-Cells's 2 digits.

description:
Here are the URLs for today's 5 GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles. Hat times are given as (two hats/one hat). Any correct solution gets you a dinosaur. 

GAS 606 – 159 Sudoku by shye https://tinyurl.com/2v726m49 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2o24mj96
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each digit in column 1 indicates which column the 1 appears in its respective row (for instance, if r3c1 was a 6, then r3c6 would be a 1). Likewise, each digit in column 5 indicates where 5 appears in the row, and each digit in column 9 indicates the 9 in the row. (7:30/15:00) (Special hat time for 12-time Times Crossword Champions is three hats for a time in 4:00 or under)

GAS 607 – Classic Sudoku by jovi_al  https://tinyurl.com/4rye48nj 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2465kfr9
Normal sudoku rules apply. And that’s it! (5:00/9:00)

GAS 608 – Renthermo by Tyrgannus https://tinyurl.com/ysbr8tyd 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=22donmw2
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer must strictly increase from the bulb to the tip. All thermos are a string of consecutive digits (such as 1-2-3 or 5-6-7-8). (7:30/12:00)

GAS 609 – Quadruples Sudoku by Freddie Hand  https://tinyurl.com/2sxez4x7 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=28eouvxb
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a white circle must appear in the four cells surrounding it (if a digit appears twice in a white circle, it must appear at least twice in the four surrounding cells)  (7:30/13:00)

GAS 610 – TomTom by Eric Fox  https://tinyurl.com/2p8j8evm 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=29rjkluo
Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue represents the value obtained by applying an operation iteratively on the numbers in the region the clue is in. If no operation is given, it may be any of +, -, ×, or ÷. Subtraction and division in regions with more than two numbers are handled by taking the largest number and subtracting/dividing all the others. (10:00/18:00)

title: The Shattered Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The rules for this sudoku begin with "the grid has been torn apart"!  It's by Panthera and it's a tribute to her father called I Love You Dad!  It's a gorgeous (and quite approachable) puzzle where you get to solve two grids and earn a picture at the end.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/8B6JdHDNpf

and a blank grid for you to make the picture with:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/93f2mdrggb

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply - but the grid has been torn apart and scrambled. The clues outside the grid indicate the sums of the contiguous runs of digits found in that 3x3 box's row/column- these digits  must be shaded. There must be an unshaded cell between runs of shaded cells. If a row/column is unclued, there is NO shading in that row/column. 3x3 boxes are numbered by convention from left to right and top to bottom such that the top left box is 1, top middle is 2, and so on. Within each box the cells are numbered in the same way. Each box must have its box number in its correct position within the box (ie box 1 of the untorn sudoku has a 1 in position 1, box 2 has 2 in position 2, etc). NO other digit in any box may be in its self-numbered cell. When finished, the shaded cells create a picture if put together in the correct order.

title: The Puzzle That Will Haunt Mark
description:
Here's where you can play Sudokoban by DiMono: https://tinyurl.com/ctcsudokuban 
In a standard sudoku grid, the boxes are numbered by convention from left to right and top to bottom such that the top left box is box 1, top middle is box 2, and so on. Within each box, the cells are numbered the same way. In this puzzle, the boxes have been separated and shuffled around, and it is up to the solver to determine their actual placement in the solution. Each box must have its box number in that position within the box (i.e. box 1 has 1 in position 1, box 2 has 2 in position 2, etc). No other digit in any box may be in its self-numbered cell.
Fill each box with the digits 1-9 so that when the boxes are restored to their proper positions, each digit appears exactly once in each box, resulting row, and resulting column. Digits in a cage must sum to the indicated number. For a clue outside a box with no arrow, the first X cells, where X is the first seen digit, sum to the value of the clue. ? sums must be deduced by the solver. Sums do not cross box gaps. A clue with an arrow shows the sum of the indicated diagonal. Diagonals do not cross box gaps.

title: The Most Popular Japanese Puzzle Is...?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
There is one puzzle type that is exceptionally popular but, if you not from Japan, you might not have heard of it.  It's called Akari (or Lights Up) and, when the website Nikoli was up-and-running, the Akari puzzles were always the most popular.  Now Jay Dyer has made a puzzle that merges Akari and Sudoku in her usual brilliant manner.  It's called Even Lighting and you can play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/PnnNbp7GHR

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.Some cells (to be located by the solver) are doublers, and have a value equal to double their digit.The even-valued cells (including doublers) form a single orthogonally connected area. Every even cell must see at least one doubler in a straight line horizontally or vertically (odd-valued cells block the view). Doublers must not see each other.The values of cells in a cage sum to the total in the corner of the cage (if given). Digits may not repeat in a cage (though values may repeat).

title: The Odyssey
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Some puzzles are easy and some aren't.  This one isn't!  

Phistomefel has merged the logic problem Japanese Sums with sudoku in a sublime and mind-bending way.  The result is one of the greatest puzzles you'll ever try and features the most annoying type of clue: the asterisk - which in Japanese Sums is actually LESS useful than a chocolate teapot!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/Hb2bQ4F77T

Rules: 
Shade some of the cells and write a digit from 1 to 9 in every unshaded cell such that no digit repeats within a row or column. Shaded cells cannot contain numbers. A row or column does not necessarily contain every digit from 1 to 9. There are nine orthogonally-connected sets of unshaded cells containing each digit from 1 to 9 exactly once, in the grid. Each unshaded cell is part of such a region and the regions may not touch orthogonally, but may touch diagonally. The clues outside of the grid are “Japanese Sum” clues. A number indicates the sum of the digits in a consecutive set of unshaded cells. The clues are given in the right order. A single '?' represents a single digit from 1 to 9. Combined with another digit, it can also be 0, as long as it is not the leading digit. E.g. '1?' could be any number from 10 to 19 and '?4' can be 14, 24, 34 or 44. '??' represents some number which is greater than 9. '*' represents any number of sets of consecutive unshaded cells with arbitrary sums including no unshaded cells at all. Every consecutive set of unshaded cell is accounted for by Japanese Sum clues.

The poem Departure mentioned at the start of the video is by Brian Bilson, who appears on Twitter at

title: The Illegal Sudoku Cage
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An absolute cracker today from Cris Moore in the form of his Square Dance - a puzzle which teaches some simple arithmetic and some gorgeous logic.  How do these strangely numbered cages work?!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/F2LtPfMmLQ

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cage totals are shown in the upper left corner of the cage. Inequalities between cells point to the small of the two digits. Nine cells in the grid are “multipliers”. If a multiplier appears in a cage, then it multiplies the sum of the other digits in the cage to produce the cage total. For instance, if a cage contains 3, 4, 5, 6 and 3 is the multiplier, the cage total would be 3*(4+5+6)=45. A multiplier which is not in a cage has no effect. Each row, each column, and each 3x3 box contains one multiplier, and each digit appears as a multiplier once.

title: The "Worst" Puzzle We've Ever Featured
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The question of how puzzles end up with the ratings they do is a vexed and interesting one. Myxo's sudoku, Revolver, has perhaps the lowest rating of any we've featured on the channel.  And yet... it is startlingly brilliant.  All hail the CTC Testers who have unearthed another stunner!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/QQdj4f9nrP

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits may not repeat within a cage. Every digit, except the digit in the centre (r5c5), has a 'partner digit' that is always placed in the cell 180° rotationally symmetrical to its own, rotated around the centre of the grid. Which digits are paired up must be deduced by the solver. (eg If the digits 1 and 2 turned out to be a rotational pair and r2c4 is a 1, r8c6 must be a 2.)

title: Is This Sudoku Expert Trolling Us?!
description:
A quick recommendation before we get on to today's sudoku.  Two day's ago we featured a puzzle - Madrigal by Fafrd - that's proving incredibly popular.  We described it (with good reason) as The Greatest Discovery In Sudoku History so do check it out!

https://youtu.be/kDPTNACpJuA

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
One of our favourite constructors returns to the channel today with what must surely be a tongue-in-cheek sudoku?!  It's called XY Difference Sudoku and, as some of you will know, such puzzles have grids which are typically populated by diamonds.  Here we have no such help - no diamonds - in fact it is only the absence of diamonds that will help you solve this!!

There's a little bonus music at the end of today's video too.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/L8t8jQ7Ljn

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  If there's a diamond between two horizontally adjacent cells, then the absolute value of their difference is the same as the first digit in that row.  If there's a diamond between two vertically adjacent cells then the absolute value of their difference is the same as the first digit in that column. All possible diamonds are given. (Note that because there are no diamonds shown in this puzzle, there are no adjacent pairs whose difference equals the first digit in their row/column).

title: The Pawn's Gambit
description:
A quick recommendation before we get on to today's sudoku.  Two day's ago we featured a puzzle - Madrigal by Fafrd - that's proving incredibly popular.  We described it (with good reason) as The Greatest Discovery In Sudoku History so do check it out!

https://youtu.be/kDPTNACpJuA

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
HalfBakedLunatic has mashed up chess and sudoku in this hybrid puzzle called The Pawn's Gambit!  One solver described it as the "nicest use of Chess pieces ever integrated into a sudoku".

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/N888QBFmpJ

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb end. Kings are 1, Rooks are 2, Bishops are 3, Knights are 4. No King can be “in check”. Ie No two Kings can be a “Kings Move” apart; no King can be a “Knight’s Move” from any Knight; no King can be on the same diagonal as a Bishop, unless a Knight, Rook, or Pawn is blocking the path; no King can be in the same row or column as a Rook unless a Knight, Bishop, or Pawn is blocking the path; pawns moving down the board are 5. No King can be on a diagonal in the row below a downward moving pawn. Pawns moving up the board are 6. No King can be on a diagonal in the row above an upward moving pawn.

title: Battling with Snowballs
description:
Here's where you can try Snowballs by Nordy: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/T8mg9QGpdf 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each blue circle in the grid is a Snowball. Snowballs roll in straight lines—either horizontally or vertically—through a set of orthogonally connected cells. The total length (in cells) of a Snowball's path is given by the number in the top left corner of its starting cell. The digits along a Snowball's path behave as follows: after the first two digits, each digit is the sum of the two preceding digits (just like the Fibonacci Sequence). Snowballs may cross paths, and therefore may share one or more cells with other Snowballs.

description:
Here's where you can play Double Fireworks by Antiknight: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/fbqQB8jrhn 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits along each arrow must multiply to the digit in the circled cell. Nine cells in the grid (one per row, column and 3x3 box) are Doublers, which count as double their value on arrows. Each digit appears in exactly one Doubler. Doublers aren't necessarily on arrows. The value of the Doubler is counted if it appears on a one cell arrow. Eg if r7c6 is a 3 and a Doubler then r6c5 is a 6.

title: A Spooky Patterned Stone
description:
Here's where you can play Staurolite by Bellsita and Dumediat: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/76PJ4T2JtF 
PLEASE WATCH THE RULES EXPLANATION IN THE VIDEO IF YOU’RE NOT SURE WHAT THE FOLLOWING RULES MEAN! 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells connected by a V must sum to either 5 or 15. Cells connected by an X must sum to either 10 or 15. Not all possible Vs and Xs are given. Cages are psycho look-and-say cages. In these cages, the digits in the cage point to boxes in the grid, and provide a referred cell which is in the same position in both boxes. The number in the top left corner should be read as a look-and-say number, which says the number of times a digit appears in the cells referenced by that cage (eg, a '23' clue means there are two 3s in the referenced cells). Digits placed within cages do NOT count towards the look-and-say total unless they are self-referencing, and digits may NOT repeat in cages. For example, if r1c5 were a 4 and r2c5 were a 5, then exactly one of the referenced cells in box 4 or box 5 (r4c2 or r5c5, respectively) would need to contain a 2 to satisfy the look-and-say clue of '12' (ie, one 2 in the referred cells).

A couple of weeks ago, Simon solved one of the best sudokus we've ever seen: Chaotic Equality by Knickolas.  We're delighted to tell you that Knickolas has made a special video explaining how he created this incredible puzzle.

Rules: 
Divide the grid into nine regions, each consisting of nine orthogonally-connected cells. Each row, column and region must contain the digits 1 to 9 once each. Each line must pass through at least two regions.  A “line segment” consists of the digits along the line within a region from the point that line starts in that region to when it next leaves it (or ends).  The sum of digits along each line segment along a line must be the same.  Different lines can have different line segment totals. Digits in a circle indicate the number of cells that are part of a line in that cell's region.

title: The Modifier Mystery
description:
Here's where you can try Modifier Mystery by mnasti2: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/B44HPbbdfn 
Normal sudoku rules apply. One cell in each row, column, and box contains a modifier. Each of the digits 1-9 is modified once. A modifier affects the value of a cell for purposes of all clue types besides normal sudoku. Four of the modifiers double the digit in that cell. Four of the modifiers increase the digit in that cell by 1. One modifier is broken and leaves the digit in that cell unchanged. Values in cells joined by a white dot are consecutive. Values in cells joined by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. Values in cells separated by a V must sum to 5. A digit in a grey square is even. Values in the cage sum to the total given. Values along an arrow sum to the number in the attached circle. Values along a thermometer must strictly increase from bulb to tip. Neighbouring Values along a green line must differ by at least 5. Values along the orange line read the same forwards and backwards. Values along a purple line must form a set of consecutive values in any order.

description:

Normal sudoku rules apply.  Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in the arrow's circle.  The following rules apply to the colored lines (from left to right): Red = Entropic - any 3 consecutive digits will have a low (1-3), medium (4-6) and high (7-9) digit; Orange = Dutch Whispers - adjacent digits must differ by at least 4; Yellow = Palindrome - the digits read the same forwards or backwards ; Green = German Whispers - adjacent digits must differ by at least 5; Blue = Region Sums - for each box this line passes through, the digits sum to the same total; Indigo = Bounded - the first/last digits on this line are the minimum and maximum (i.e: 1,1,2,3); Violet = Renban - this line contains a set of consecutive non-repeating digits in any order.

title: The Earthquakes: A Sudoku Appeal
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We're sure all of you have seen the dreadful pictures from Turkey and Syria over the last few days following the two huge earthquakes on 6 February.  Turkey is a nation full of incredible puzzlers, including Serkan Yurekli - one of the most famous constructors in the world. Serkan has made today's puzzle with the hope that it will encourage people to help his homeland.  It's an astonishing sudoku in which he's been able to  construct an amazing logic problem out of the actual cities affected by the disaster.  Please be warned it is an emotionally challenging puzzle to solve.

Here is the url of a charity Serkan recommends:

https://ahbap.org/disasters-turkey

Please do help if you can.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/4dHgHjFHdT

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. 10 cities have been affected by two major earthquakes (7.7 and 7.6 on the Richter Scale) in Turkey. Place each city’s name along a grey line, one letter per cell. For lines without arrows, the city can be read in either direction, otherwise it must read in the arrow's direction. The sudoku works as follows: If a cell’s letter is included in the spelling of one of the digits 1 to 9 (eg ONE, TWO, etc), such a digit is a valid candidate for that cell. If a cell’s letter is not included in the spelling of ANY of the digits 1 to 9, any digit can be placed in that cell. One of the red (earthquake) lines is 7.7 and the other 7.6.  The cities to be placed are: ADANA, ADIYAMAN, DIYARBAKIR, GAZIANTEP, HATAY, KAHRAMANMARAS, KILIS, MALATYA, OSMANIYE and SANLIURFA.

GM Puzzles produces puzzles under a CC licence (https://tinyurl.com/3pj3byec). No changes have been made to this puzzle.

title: Would You Give Your Math Teacher 100%?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
American Math teacher RockyRoer's latest sudoku has been awarded 100% by its solvers on Logic Masters Germany.  And we now understand why!  This simple twist on the Sandwich Sudoku ruleset (combined with a little indexing) has resulted in an absolute banger.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/fB8pgbJ27d

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. In each row, column and 3x3 box are two 'crusts'. All nine 1s are crusts, as well as nine other cells, which could be any digit. The clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits between the two crust cells in that row or column. The capsules contain the coordinates of each of the nine crust cells that are not 1s. No two capsules refer to the same crust cell. For example, if R9C12 contains 4 and 5, than that means R4C5 is a crust cell that isn't 1.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Unusually Mark tested today's puzzle, Qi Manifest by Xendari.  To say he enjoyed it would be an understatement and so, in this video, Simon has a go at it.  Let's just say it's awesome!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/Bfd43TJgMP

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade the grid using two colours, such that all instances of each colour are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 area is completely one colour. Blue lines must have an equal sum N within each colour they pass through. If a blue line passes through a colour multiple times, each individual pass sums to N. title: Simply One Of The Best Sudokus Ever
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Let's start with what we know:  Jay Dyer is a genius.  She has done it again with a sudoku so ludicrously clever it almost defies belief.  From it's brain-breaking opening to its finishing flourish, this is simply one of the most incredible puzzles of all time.
 
Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/H87DjDq3H9

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Nine cells (one in each row, column and 3x3 box) are “doublers”, and have a value equal to double their digit. Each digit appears in exactly one doubler. The values of cells in a cage sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits may not repeat in a cage (though values may repeat). In row N (for all N from 1 to 9), the values of cells in the pill (read from left to right) give the row and column number of the doubler with the digit N.

title: Area 81: Is The Truth Actually Out There?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Today we try and absolutely great puzzle by Math Pesto called Area 81.  It builds on a type of logic puzzle called Area 51 made popular by puzzlemaker David Millar, which combines Cave, Slitherlink and Masyu.  Our only worry about this one was whether the rules might be a little tricky for new viewers to understand.  We really hope not because this is just wonderful.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/7TLdN2MJRh

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a non-intersecting loop along some edges of the grid. Aliens are inside the loop and cacti are outside the loop. A digit in a white square indicates the number of that cell’s edges that are part of the loop.  A digit in a white circle is inside the loop and indicates the number of cells inside the loop “seen” horizontally and vertically, including the circled cell itself. Cells outside the loop obstruct vision. The loop passes through a white dot in a straight line, then makes a 90-degree turn on one or both of the nearest cell corners along the loop. The loop makes a 90-degree turn on a black dot, and does not turn at the next opportunity in either direction. Diagonally adjacent cells joined by a white dot contain consecutive digits and by a black dot contain digits in a 1:2 ratio.

title: The Most Incredible Sudoku Rules EVER
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A couple of weeks ago we noted that this puzzle had been recommended to us a lot - by folks who enjoy a hearty dose of schadenfreude!  It's called Pathfinder and it's the work of KNT.  

This is one of the hardest puzzles we've ever seen, let alone solved on the channel.  It's also fair to say that for the constructor to have managed to create this sudoku using this ruleset is one of the most impressive things we've even showcased.  Apologies for the length of the video.  Apologies if Simon may have missed an option or two at a variety of points (we hope he didn't!)... but this is different gravy!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/3RJ64FJmQD

Rules: 
Divide the grid into regions, each consisting of nine orthogonally connected cells. Each row, column and region must contain the digits 1 to 9 once each. The digit in the top-left cell of a region (its leftmost cell in its highest row) is its region number. All region numbers are different. You must find an orthogonally connected path that visits every region exactly once, and the path must visit each region in ascending order of the region numbers. Within each region, digits strictly increase along the path. A digit in a cell with arrow(s) indicates the total number of cells in the same region as that cell that are part of the path, in the indicated directions combined. If a cell has multiple arrows, there must be at least one cell on the path (in the arrowed cell's region) in each of the clued directions.

An example puzzle (which we'd recommend you analyse) is available here:

https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=000BI5

title: How To See Through The Sudoku Fog
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We love Fog sudoku puzzles and today Olima entertains us with Claudia Cum Cereo Circulat (we're not certain what this means!).  This is a brilliant example of using so-called "negative constraints" in a way that adds to the solving experience.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/JHnRqh93pr

Rules:

title: The 7x7 "Blue" Square
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Adem Jaziri only needs 49 cells today to bamboozle us with a puzzle that scores top marks on the cleverness scale.  This is weird and wonderful and it takes quite some thought!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/7ttN3TmD7M

Rules: 
Fill the grid such that each row, column, and orthogonally-connected 7-cell region contains the digits 1-7 with no repeats. The regions must be determined by the solver. The sum of the digits along a blue line must be the same within each region the line passes through.  Eg if r2r3r4c6 were in one region and r5r6c6 were in a separate region, then the sum of the digits in r2r3r4c6 = the sum of the digits in r5r6c6. Adjacent digits on a green line must have a difference of at least 4.

title: One Of The Cleverest Puzzles EVER
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We are absolutely gobsmacked by this one.  It's called Chaotic Equality and it's the work of Knickolas.  If you read this Knickolas, we'd love to showcase a video on how you constructed this puzzle because it defies belief. Oh and it isn't easy!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/RjG3t8B9dp

Rules: 
Divide the grid into nine regions, each consisting of nine orthogonally-connected cells. Each row, column and region must contain the digits 1 to 9 once each. Each line must pass through at least two regions.  A “line segment” consists of the digits along the line within a region from the point that line starts in that region to when it next leaves it (or ends).  The sum of digits along each line segment along a line must be the same.  Different lines can have different line segment totals. Digits in a circle indicate the number of cells that are part of a line in that cell's region.

title: Cracking The Cryptic: The Miracle Movie
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
With apologies to those who prefer shorter videos, Simon decides to try Agent's latest 100%-rated sudoku, Skycagers.  It's absolutely magical and quite how this puzzle resolves uniquely given the scant clues is little short of miraculous.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/nh43mpHn8M

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into cages, i.e. non-overlapping areas of one or more orthogonally connected cell(s) with no repeating digits. A clue in the top-left corner of a cell indicates the sum of digits in that cage. Some cages do not contain any clues. For these other cages, the sum must be determined by the solver. Some cells may be outside cages. No two cages can share the same sum. Each cage represents a building whose height equals the sum of its digits. Clues outside the grid indicate the number of buildings “seen” from that direction. Taller buildings block the view of smaller buildings. Cells outside cages cannot be seen.
